headnotes.la: …, sancti nimirum angeli, qui voluntatem ejus apud se continua stabilitate custodiunt, et ob hoc amici sunt; quique ipsius visione assidue perfruuntur, et ob hoc, vicini recte nominantur; quibus dicet,
headnotes.en: …who keep his will with them in unbroken steadfastness, and for this reason are friends; and who enjoy his vision without ceasing, and for this reason are rightly named neighbours; to whom he will say,

headnotes.la: … de sua restauratione gratulanti sponso, gratulanti etiam virtutum supernarum multitudini, congratulabitur. Implebitur ipsa die, quod in historia continetur, manifestans enim se fratribus suis Joseph,
headnotes.en: …ion, and to the multitude of the supernal virtues, which rejoices likewise. There will be fulfilled on that very day what is contained in the history: for Joseph, making himself known to his brethren,

headnotes.la: Alieni erunt ipsa die quibus dicturus est Dominus,
headnotes.en: Strangers will they be on that day to whom the Lord is to say,

headnotes.la: Quibus ea die separatis, manifestabit se Dominus Jesus fratribus suis, dicens,
headnotes.en: When these have been separated on that day, the Lord Jesus will make himself known to his brethren, saying,

headnotes.la: …us, acquisierit; et acquisitam indicibili jam gloria muneraverit, cujus quidem bonus illa die et universis applaudet, et singulis. Quid enim est illa Domini gratiarum actio, qua dicturus est illa die,
headnotes.en: …dowed her, so gained, with unspeakable glory: of which indeed the good one will on that day applaud both all and each. For what is that giving of thanks by the Lord, in which he is to say on that day,

headnotes.la: …tu, cum quis interius nullo virtutis indumento vestitur. Hoc frigus ab Aquilone est, quo corda multorum non infrigidantur solum, sed indurantur [n: (Job XXXVII, 9; Eccli. XLIII, 22)]; de quo propheta,
headnotes.en: …othed within by no garment of virtue. This cold is from the North wind, by which the hearts of many are not only chilled but hardened [n: (Job XXXVII, 9; Eccli. XLIII, 22)]; of which the prophet says,

headnotes.la: *(Psal. CXLVII, 17.)* Hanc Christi nuditatem in ejus membris operit, qui destitutum virtute virtutum exemplis informat et instruit. Cui congratulans Dominus in fine dicturus est,
headnotes.en: …17.)* This nakedness of Christ in his members he covers, who forms and instructs by the examples of the virtues the man destitute of virtue. To whom the Lord, congratulating him, is to say at the end,

headnotes.la: Quonam vero modo peregrinus et hospes in membris suis sit Dominus, palam est; in se vero peregrinus et hospes est apud eos, qui nondum fidem quae in ipsum est, susceperunt: qualibus et ipse ait,
headnotes.en: …is a stranger and a guest in his members is plain; while in himself he is a stranger and a guest among those who have not yet received the faith which is in him: to such as these he himself also says,

headnotes.la: quia tenebrosa peccantium corda immundi spiritus et fraudulenti possidentes inhabitant;
headnotes.en: because unclean and deceitful spirits, possessing them, dwell in the darkened hearts of sinners;

headnotes.la: …no a Patre genitum esse, protestantur: ipsis vero alienus, qui ipsum non idem in substantia esse cum Patre affirmare conantur). Apud hos hospes est et peregrinus; quibus omnibus per prophetam dicitur,
headnotes.en: …from eternity; and to those he is alien who attempt to affirm that he is not the same in substance with the Father). Among these he is a guest and a stranger; to all of whom it is said by the prophet,

headnotes.la: Apud hos hospes est et peregrinus, pulsans per prophetas, per apostolos, per Scripturas omnes, ut ipsi aperiant; quibus Dominus illa die dicturus est,
headnotes.en: Among these he is a guest and a stranger, knocking by the prophets, by the apostles, by all the Scriptures, that they may open to him; to whom the Lord is to say on that day,

headnotes.la: …olumbae simplices, munda tantum grana fidei colligentes; quibus quippe non satis est per fidem tantum salvatorem tecto suscipere, nisi et hunc suscipiant omnimoda charitate et virtute Ipse namque ait,
headnotes.en: …e clean grains of faith; for whom indeed it is not enough to receive the Saviour under their roof by faith only, unless they receive him also with charity and virtue of every kind For he himself says,

headnotes.la: …anti spiritualiter exhibendum est. Languor enim spiritus in multis adeo convalescit [cn: 8 | Forte *invalescit*.], ut jam in iis nec confessionis sit vox, nec sensus poenitentis. De iis ait Apostolus,
headnotes.en: … is ailing spiritually. For in many the languor of the spirit so gathers strength that in them there is now neither the voice of confession nor the feeling of one repenting. Of these the Apostle says,

headnotes.la: … sed et exterioris hominis sui plena dispositione, conformentur. Hinc enim est, quod cum Elias suscitavit mortuum [n: (III Reg. XVII, 21)], expandit se super illum: et Elisaeus dum mortuum suscitavit,
headnotes.en: …also by the full ordering of their outward man. For hence it is that when Elias raised up the dead man [n: (III Reg. XVII, 21)], he spread himself over him; and Elisha, when he raised up the dead man,

headnotes.la: Ut, sicut ait Apostolus, membra sui corporis omnia quae ante
headnotes.en: So that, as the Apostle says, those who are raised from death, by imitating the holy teachers, may now compel all the members of their body which before had been

headnotes.la: hi qui suscitantur a morte, doctores sanctos imitando, virtuti jam servire compellant De iis ipsa Veritas ait,
headnotes.en: to serve virtue Of these the Truth itself says,

headnotes.la: Horum quidem levioribus morbis, alii gravioribus et diutinis fatigantur. Hi itaque quos peccati vetustas opprimit, quasi quidam animarum carcer includit; quorum assumens in se personam propheta, ait,
headnotes.en: …es, others by heavier and long-lasting ones. And so these, whom the oldness of sin oppresses, a certain prison of souls, as it were, shuts in; whose person the prophet takes upon himself when he says,

headnotes.la: et illud,
headnotes.en: and that other word,

headnotes.la: et item,
headnotes.en: and again,

headnotes.la: …it Dominus, et expostulat: quae vero non ad proximum sunt, sed ob Christi reverentiam observantur, haec ea sunt quae Dominus in seipso esurire dicitur, et sitire, quod ipsi hoc idem est, quod et velle
headnotes.en: …se which are not toward our neighbour, but are kept for reverence of Christ, these are they which the Lord is said to hunger and thirst for in himself, since with him this is the same thing as to will

headnotes.la: et pendens in cruce, dixit,
headnotes.en: and hanging on the cross he said,

headnotes.la: … dicta verborum clausula omnes animae dotes, Ecclesiae bona generaliter omnia, comprehendi. Et hoc congratulationis est osculum in quod suspirat Ecclesia, quod in Spiritu postulat omnis anima, dicens,
headnotes.en: …all the endowments of the soul, all the goods of the Church generally, are comprehended. And this is the kiss of congratulation for which the Church sighs, which every soul asks in the Spirit, saying,

headnotes.la: Sic ad Patrem loquens, os ejus, juxta hunc sensum. Filium nominans et tam ipsius Patris quam Filii osculum, Spiritum sanctum intelligens. Ait enim,
headnotes.en: Thus she speaks to the Father, his mouth, according to this sense. Naming the Son, and understanding by the kiss both of the Father himself and of the Son the Holy Spirit. For she says,

headnotes.la: Pater, id est me dignam osculo, ipse qui creavit, efficiat; et hoc,
headnotes.en: that is, let the Father, he who created me, make me worthy of the kiss; and this,

headnotes.la: …dat Pater, osculum quod dat Filius; quia vapor est, et procedens ab utroque suavitas: qui sicut ab utroque procedit, sic et Pater ipsum et Filius in beatorum corda diffundit. De ipso enim ait Dominus,
headnotes.en: …es; because he is a vapour, and a sweetness proceeding from both: who, as he proceeds from both, so both the Father and the Son pour him forth into the hearts of the blessed. For of him the Lord says,

headnotes.la: et alibi,
headnotes.en: and elsewhere,

headnotes.la: …ovum quemdam decorem transeat, ut in illa die, a Patre per Filium vocem congratulationis audiat, et osculum congratulationis accipiat. Vox enim congratulationis est, qua Dominus illa die dicturus est,
headnotes.en: …hat day she may hear from the Father through the Son the voice of congratulation, and receive the kiss of congratulation. For it is the voice of congratulation by which the Lord is to say on that day,

headnotes.la: et illa ad Virtutes coelestes,
headnotes.en: and that word to the heavenly Virtues,

headnotes.la: …sae congratulationem, in aeternum futura est, manifesta quaedam demonstratio est. Voluptas enim, quaedam foeda est, quaedam vero sanctissima: et illa quidem sancta est, cujus meminit Propheta, dicens,
headnotes.en: …idegroom's congratulation upon the goods of the Bride, is to be forever. For pleasure is of one sort foul, and of another most holy: and that indeed is holy of which the Prophet makes mention, saying,

headnotes.la: quae quidem voluptas
headnotes.en: which pleasure indeed is called a

headnotes.la: dicitur, non quod cito transeat, sed quod abundanter infundat. De hac enim et
headnotes.en: , not because it passes quickly away, but because it pours itself in abundantly. For of this also

headnotes.la: Juxta quod
headnotes.en: According to which

headnotes.la: ait,
headnotes.en: says,

headnotes.la: Unde et convenienter Propheta ait,
headnotes.en: Whence the Prophet also fittingly says,

headnotes.la: …endetur, in illum mens tota se colliget; patrem nesciet, ignorabit et matrem; erga neminem affectione tangetur, nisi quem Christo conformem noverit, quem corpori ejus compaginatum et unitum adverterit
headnotes.en: …he will be ignorant of a mother also; she will be touched with affection toward no one save him whom she has known to be conformed to Christ, whom she has perceived to be joined and united to his body

headnotes.la: et ipse erit
headnotes.en: and he himself shall be

headnotes.la: …quitatis gradus esse poterunt. His omnibus felici jam commercio commutatis, ut horum loco quae in carne habuimus, jam et secundum carnem patrem Deum habeamus; ut ipse nobis sufficiens voluptas sit, et
headnotes.en: …n exchanged in a happy commerce, so that in place of those which we had in the flesh we may now have God as father even according to the flesh; that he himself may be for us a sufficient pleasure, and

headnotes.la: …ret. Thesauros itaque sapientiae et scientiae ingrediens, totum quod ornare et beatificare mentem potest, invenit affluenter; ut nil ei jam desit in ulla gratia, sed confidenter jam dicat Domino Jesu,
headnotes.en: …ures of wisdom and knowledge, it finds in overflowing measure all that can adorn and beatify the mind; so that nothing is now lacking to it in any grace, but it says confidently now to the Lord Jesus,

headnotes.la: …rsum jam consummasse laetabitur. Hoc voluptatis est osculum, quod de loco voluptatis quem plantaverat Dominus a principio, dari sibi sancta Ecclesia, dari sibi fidelis anima quaeque desiderat, dicens,
headnotes.en: … kiss of pleasure which, out of the place of pleasure which the Lord had planted from the beginning, the holy Church desires to be given her, which every faithful soul desires to be given her, saying,

headnotes.la: Modo itaque mirabili, statim in operis ipso principio meminit finis, dicens,
headnotes.en: And so in a wondrous manner, at the very beginning of the work she makes mention at once of the end, saying,

headnotes.la: …iritus aestuantem, statim Sponsus advertit: et quia spes quae differtur affligit animam, ne affligat eamdem, et spem ejus in longum protrahendo differat, sic desideranti respondet; fiet quod postulas,
headnotes.en: …f spirit: and because hope that is deferred afflicts the soul, lest it afflict her and, by drawing out her hope at length, defer it, he answers her thus as she desires: what thou askest shall be done,

headnotes.la: …dere, ab homicidio, adulterio, et furto, et falso testimonio, et ab iis omnibus quae Lege prohibentur, abstinere? voluntarie vero et malitiose peccantibus, lac acidum Lex ipsa proponit, hoc annectens,
headnotes.en: …urder, adultery, and theft, and false witness, and from all those things which are forbidden by the Law? But to those who sin willingly and maliciously the Law itself sets forth sour milk, adding this

headnotes.la: Quod quidem lac patienti videtur acidum, sed Regi bono, et secundum timorem Dei constituto Principi, lac placidum est, et gustu suavissimum; quia,
headnotes.en: Which milk indeed seems sour to him who suffers, but to a good King, and to a Prince established according to the fear of God, it is a soothing milk and most sweet to the taste; because,

headnotes.la: … et in coagulum, in caseum, et serum: haec virtutum gradus enunciant, quibus a minimo ad perfectum ascendendum est. Serum enim, quod sero de lacte colligitur, ipse est timor Domini, de quo dictum est,
headnotes.en: …rees of the virtues, by which one must ascend from the least to the perfect. For the whey (*serum*), which is gathered late (*sero*) from the milk, is itself the fear of the Lord, of which it is said,

headnotes.la: …; regnum quoque ejus, et vitam, quae fine caritura est, bonis omnibus repromittens. Omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum hujus dulcedine lactis exhilarat. Caeteris tamen lac acidum propinat, dicens,
headnotes.en: …ngdom, and the life which will be without end, to all the good. It gladdens every man coming into this world with the sweetness of this milk. To the rest, however, it gives sour milk to drink, saying,

headnotes.la: Quo in loco,
headnotes.en: In which place, threatening

headnotes.la: septies interminans, lac illud innuit, quod vere in dentium stuporem acidum, in fine reprobis omnibus daturus est, dicens,
headnotes.en: seven times, he hints at that milk, sour indeed to the setting of the teeth on edge, which he is to give at the end to all the reprobate, saying,

headnotes.la: …ero dextro illae assignatae sunt, quae mundum, et ea quae mundi sunt, spernere, ejus delicias abhorrere, Deum solum diligere, hunc appetere, hinc dissolvi, et esse cum Christo, persuadent. Unde illud,
headnotes.en: …ersuade us to despise the world and the things which are of the world, to shrink from its delights, to love God alone, to long for him, to be dissolved hence and to be with Christ. Whence that saying,

headnotes.la: … quae hujusmodi sunt, uberi dextro recte competunt. His igitur uberibus ditata Sponsa alit populos, et primis enutritos virtutibus ad summa et perfecta perducit; et ei recte Sponsus applaudit, dicens,
headnotes.en: …Enriched, therefore, with these breasts, the Bride feeds peoples, and leads those nourished in the first virtues to the highest and perfect things; and rightly does the Bridegroom applaud her, saying,

headnotes.la: …mus, et involvit? adeo ut quae Dei sunt negligat, et ea quae Dei sunt, haec inquirere et investigare contemnat. Has quis enumeret? has quis sub numero comprehendat? Artes quidem septem sunt, quae ideo
headnotes.en: …od's, and scorns to seek out and search into those things which are God's. Who could number these? who could comprehend them under a number? The arts indeed are seven, which are for this reason called

headnotes.la: …um, ab eo longe est qui simplex est veritas, sanctam praebens Evangelii et sine fuco scientiam. Quid arithmeticae numeros, Musicae consonantias aut dissonantias, geometriae figuras enumerem? in quibus
headnotes.en: … simple truth, offering the holy knowledge of the Gospel and without paint. Why should I enumerate the numbers of arithmetic, the consonances or dissonances of music, the figures of geometry? in which

headnotes.la: dicente Sapientia,
headnotes.en: since Wisdom says,

headnotes.la: Sunt et artes quae
headnotes.en: There are also the arts which are called

headnotes.la: …at ea quae Dei sunt: et an incarnatus Deus, an passus, an resurrexit, et ascendit, et mortalibus aeterna promiserit, aut prorsus ignorat, aut forte nota despiciat. Sed Sponsae quid de iis Sponsus ait?
headnotes.en: …rose again and ascended and promised eternal things to mortals, it is either utterly ignorant, or perhaps despises what it knows. But what does the Bridegroom say to the Bride concerning these things?

headnotes.la: protestans longe fore melius lacte Ecclesiae simpliciter enutriri, quam iis quae dicta sunt, superbe et inutiliter inebriari. Hinc Isaias ait,
headnotes.en: declaring that it is far better to be nourished simply by the milk of the Church than to be proudly and uselessly made drunk with the things which have been named. Hence Isaias says,

headnotes.la: [n: (Isa. LV, 2.)] Argentum enim non in panibus expendere, est eloquentiam et laborem in iis consumere, quae Dei notitiam et visionem non dant: de qua ait David,
headnotes.en: [n: (Isa. LV, 2.)] For to spend silver not upon bread is to consume eloquence and labour upon those things which do not give the knowledge and the vision of God: of which David says,

headnotes.la: Cur vero meliora reputari debent, causam annectit, dicens, Quia sunt
headnotes.en: But why they ought to be reckoned better, he adds the cause, saying, Because they are

headnotes.la: …que dolet, admisisse quempiam id quod luget: post ejulatum, et confessionem, et satisfactionis opera, spes jam mitigat id quod dolebat: hinc charitas in vitam aeternam, ea quae sunt solidata conservat
headnotes.en: …nts: after the wailing, and the confession, and the works of satisfaction, hope now soothes that which was painful: hence charity preserves unto eternal life the things which have been made solid. The

headnotes.la: ergo Ecclesiae,
headnotes.en: therefore of the Church

headnotes.la: id est, simplices illae doctrinae quae ab uberibus eliciuntur Ecclesiae, potentiores, et ad animae salutem efficaciores sunt
headnotes.en: that is, those simple teachings which are drawn out from the breasts of the Church are mightier and more effectual unto the soul's salvation than the

headnotes.la: id est, figmentis omnibus et inventionibus, quae secularis adinvenit sapientia, ut iis, sequentes se, et sibi dantes operam, potet et inebriet: ideoque
headnotes.en: that is, than all the figments and inventions which secular wisdom has found out, that with them it may give drink to and inebriate those following it and giving their labour to it: and therefore

headnotes.la: Haec Sponsae ad Sponsum est amicabilis et honesta responsio. Gratificavit eam suo nuper Sponsus elogio, dicens
headnotes.en: This is the Bride's friendly and honourable answer to the Bridegroom. The Bridegroom lately gratified her with his commendation, saying

headnotes.la: Quae et illi velut gratias agens, hoc ei respondit elogio, dicens,
headnotes.en: And she, as though giving him thanks, answered him with this commendation, saying,

headnotes.la: …ti nomine signata et fundata, et apostolorum documentis est denunciata, omnibus quae adversus hanc invensionibus jam dictae sunt, vel forte poterunt inveniri, superesse et praevalere: unde et dicitur,
headnotes.en: …eachings of the apostles, remains above and prevails over all the inventions [sic: *invensionibus*] against it which have already been named, or which perhaps may yet be found: whence it is also said,

headnotes.la: id est, fides quae in nomine tuo est, sic est ut oleum. Quod ut magis exprimat, adjicitur,
headnotes.en: that is, the faith which is in thy name is thus as oil. And that she may express this the more, there is added,

headnotes.la: …r hunc incarnari constituit; et oleum de ramo hoc expressum, tam late per mundum effudit, quam latissime incarnatio haec toti mundo multis variisque modis innotuit. Hoc innumeris unctione sua profuit;
headnotes.en: …om this branch he poured forth as widely through the world as this incarnation was made known most widely to the whole world in many and various ways. This profited men beyond number by its anointing;

headnotes.la: Quid iis enarrandis immorer? Joannem audiamus dicentem,
headnotes.en: Why should I linger in the telling of these things? Let us hear John, saying,

headnotes.la: …ttenda, signorum. Hujus enim effusio olei mundum illuminat. Ecclesiae faciem exhilarat, cibos aptat et praeparat; ut sine hujus admistione, suo vix cibo spiritus satiari praevaleat. Nam ut Paulus ait,
headnotes.en: …the world. It gladdens the face of the Church, it fits and prepares her food; so that without the mingling of this, the spirit can scarcely prevail to be satisfied with its own food. For as Paul says,

headnotes.la: …ae cibos animae condit, aptat, et praeparat, ut in fide oblata placeant; et quantumcunque minima, magna tamen sunt, et a Deo magnum quidem regnum, scilicet, coelorum obtinentia. Recte ergo dictum est,
headnotes.en: …hings offered in faith may please; and however small they be, they are nevertheless great, and obtain from God a kingdom truly great, namely of the heavens. Rightly therefore has it been said that the

headnotes.la: Christi, id est, fidem ejus, in qua nos salvari oportet,
headnotes.en: of Christ, that is, his faith, in which we must be saved, is

headnotes.la: …um transmutantem, deinde in monte transfigurantem se, facieque in modum Solis resplendente, in vestimentis etiam candorem nivis exhibentem, cum mortuis colloquia habentem, Patremque de nube testantem,
headnotes.en: …lf on the mountain, with his face shining in the manner of the Sun, showing also in his garments the whiteness of snow, holding converse with the dead, and the Father bearing witness out of the cloud,

headnotes.la: …sime manifesta suscepta morte immortalitate de ipsa triumphantem, sicque ad coelos unde venerat redeuntem; quid nisi Deum credere, venerari, et adorare, et super omnia diligere, potuerunt? Hunc itaque
headnotes.en: … in immortality over that death itself, and so returning to the heavens whence he had come; what could they do but believe him God, venerate and adore him, and love him above all things? Him therefore

headnotes.la: id est animae nuper ad fidem conversae: qualem animam fuisse Petri in primis aestimo, cum dixit,
headnotes.en: that is, the souls lately converted to the faith: and such a soul I judge Peter's to have been at the first, when he said,

headnotes.la: …evit, post in juvenem firmissimum, et sic in virum perfectum evasit. De Paulo etiam persecutore quid referam? qui nunc persecutor, nunc adolescentulus effectus est, illustrante eum Domino, et dicente,
headnotes.en: …ng man, and so came forth into a perfect man. And of Paul the persecutor what shall I relate? who at one moment a persecutor, at the next was made a little youth, the Lord enlightening him and saying,

headnotes.la: Ad hanc statim vocem vere conversus est, dicens,
headnotes.en: At this voice he was straightway truly converted, saying,

headnotes.la: …ilia intellexerunt, quibus nec resistere, nec contradicere poterunt, id verbo, id opere protestati sunt, nomen hoc solum adorandum esse, et prae cunctis quae sub coelo sunt, diligendum: unde subditur,
headnotes.en: …ey will be able neither to resist nor to gainsay, protested, by word and by work, that this name alone is to be adored, and to be loved before all things which are under heaven: whence there is added,

headnotes.la: …ut ipsa in membris suis minimis pertrahatur ad Patrem; optans ut secum omnes occurramus in virum perfectum, et mensuram aetatis plenitudinis Christi [n: (Ephes. IV, 13)]; unde et subdit quod sequitur,
headnotes.en: …to the Father; wishing that we may all together meet with her unto a perfect man, and the measure of the age of the fulness of Christ [n: (Ephes. IV, 13)]; whence also she subjoins that which follows,

headnotes.la: …s semper operibus implicatus, in iis vitam consumit. In dextram vero trahitur, cui bonus praeest angelus, ostendens ei bona quae faciat, et his consummandis semper intendat: unde ad Deum loquens, ait,
headnotes.en: … But he is drawn to the right over whom a good angel presides, showing him the good things that he should do, and to the finishing of these let him always be intent: whence, speaking to God, she says,

headnotes.la: id est, in iis qui tibi placita sunt, in quibus te praeducem habeam, in iis me detine, nec aberrare me, vel alias deflectere me permittas: sic enim scriptum est,
headnotes.en: …hose things which are pleasing to thee, in which I may have thee as my leader before me, in those things keep me, and suffer me neither to stray nor to be turned aside elsewhere: for so it is written,

headnotes.la: Ut ergo accedamus ad Deum, Patre trahente opus est, ut nos ipse praeveniat, sic [cn: 11 | Forte *se*.] ducem praebeat, et cum duxerit, ipse suscipiat. Item quoque scriptum legimus,
headnotes.en: …pproach to God, there is need of the Father drawing, that he himself may go before us, may so present himself as leader, and, when he has led, may himself receive us. Likewise also we read it written,

headnotes.la: … petit, qui trahitur, et levare se super se totus intendit, virtutum montem coram se conspicit, et dum ejus ardua apprehendere nititur, in imo se quandoque conspicit, et miratur. Clamat itaque dicens,
headnotes.en: …ve himself; he beholds before him the mountain of the virtues, and while he strives to lay hold of its steep places, he beholds himself at times in the depth, and wonders. And so he cries out, saying,

headnotes.la: quia de valle hac non ascendo, nisi per te. Quod si porrectam tibi manum Dei senseris, et extractum de valle miseriarum, et de luto faecis agnoveris, manum apprehende, tene, deosculare, et dic,
headnotes.en: …lt have felt the hand of God stretched out to thee, and shalt have recognized thyself drawn out of the valley of miseries and out of the mire of dregs, lay hold of the hand, hold it, kiss it, and say,

headnotes.la: … peccatis, sanctorum se moribus applicet, hos imitando se sanctificet, et odore perfusus unguentorum spiritualium, in his semper gaudeat, securus oblectetur et quiescat. Obsecrat igitur in hunc modum,
headnotes.en: …, may sanctify himself by imitating them, and, drenched with the odor of spiritual ointments, may always rejoice in them, may securely take his delight, and rest. He entreats therefore in this manner,

headnotes.la: id est, Tu, ad quem non venitur nisi per te, mihi funem tui amoris innecte, quo pertrahar ad te, quo alias [cn: 12-13 | *qui alio*.] divertere non sinat me. Ait enim Salomon, quia
headnotes.en: that is, Thou, to whom none comes save by thee, knit for me the rope of thy love, whereby I may be drawn to thee, whereby it may not suffer me to turn aside elsewhere. For Solomon says that

headnotes.la: …ris, ut cor meum cogitando mala pertrahat ad se, linguam meam haec loquendo totam inflammet ex se, et corpus meum haec agendo inclinet totum et divertat ad se; quid mihi, nisi ut dicam illud apostoli?
headnotes.en: …y speaking these things inflame my whole tongue out of itself, and by doing these things bend my whole body and turn it aside to itself; what is there for me, save that I say that word of the apostle?

headnotes.en: [n: (Rom. VII, 24.)] Do thou, O Lord, answer me,

headnotes.en: That is, being snatched from the malignant one by thee, stirred to the good by thee, brought to the highest by thy drawing,

headnotes.en: that is, we shall go forward our whole life long;

headnotes.la: … quod in cellariis est, in cellariis exultat: et sunt quidem cellaria divini palatii pars aliqua, opes in se regis continens, et secreta. Regis vero palatium illud est, cujus meminit propheta, dicens,

headnotes.la: …tendamus palatium, quod utique tantum est, quantum creatura protenditur. Ejus longum, latum, et altum, omnis emetitur creaturae dimensionem. Quod si mente procedas ulterius, audi Scripturam; ait enim,

headnotes.en: …eby he should have an end; but where he appoints the boundary of the creature, there he receives himself in his own simplicity and purity: according to which the Truth testifies in the Gospel, saying,

headnotes.la: Hoc itaque regis palatium est; et sunt ejus cellaria, mansiones quaedam coelestes, quarum meminit Dominus, dicens,
headnotes.en: This therefore is the palace of the king; and its cellars are certain heavenly mansions, of which the Lord makes mention, saying,

headnotes.la: …tio, et eorum perenni fruitur et jucundatur obsequio: horum naturam scit trinitas sancta, scit numerum in trinitate persona secunda, Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui cum ad passionem duceretur, ait,

headnotes.en: … and may cherish his praise without intermission, and may show that she takes her delight not in the affluence of temporal and passing things, but rather in the continual frequenting of these; saying,

headnotes.en: for vain alike is exultation, and vain is gladness, save that which is founded in the Lord: whence the Psalmist says,

headnotes.en: And likewise he begins a Psalm, saying

headnotes.en: …easts of the Bridegroom himself: and by what reason this is true must be considered. For the Bridegroom, in the first answer of his, answered the Bride above, Thy prayer is not to be repelled, because

headnotes.en: …racles; which indeed are God's, divinely inspired by him: and they are the Church's, granted to her out of the grace of God for the nourishing and instructing of the peoples. This Bride therefore says

headnotes.la: id est divinorum eloquiorum, quae a te inspirata sunt, et a te mihi dante concessa
headnotes.en: that is, of the divine oracles, which have been inspired by thee, and granted to me by thy giving

headnotes.en: …as created, who is stretched out with his whole body thither whence it has been granted him to be, to live, to be wise, and to understand. Whence is this to any man, save from God? For the Psalm says,

headnotes.la: …io tendit, unde sibi ista adesse recognoscat: qui vero deorsum flectitur, qui ad mundum inclinatur, caput deorsum figens, pedes sursum erigens, monstro assimilatur, et curvus est; de quo propheta ait,

headnotes.en: …re of form, more of comeliness, more of honor and of seemliness, than all that which allures the sight, which snatches to itself and distracts the affections of mortals: for thence there is subjoined,

headnotes.en: …thee as an example, stand fast, drawing near to the service of God, lest thou be easily moved; because out of this blackness an unspeakable form of comeliness shall come to thee: for so it is written,

headnotes.la: Quae quidem forma hinc primo est, quod ad imaginem et similitudinem Dei homo creatus est;
headnotes.en: Which form indeed is first from this, that man was created to the image and likeness of God;

headnotes.en: from reason;

headnotes.en: …im; whom. whosoever is well in his wits understands to lack nothing whereby the life of men may be adorned. To this skin therefore holy Church, or any perfected soul, rightly compares herself, saying,

headnotes.en: …asten him to the cross. Resigning this life, they were given over into a reprobate sense, and they who received it received power to be the sons of God: according to that which is said in the prophet,

headnotes.en: …n hope to the joys of the heavens promised to her. Hence, that she may be made the more certain, and that no one may be held doubtful in himself concerning that hope, she sends forth a prayer, saying,

headnotes.en: …oward them: whence, because among the heavenly gifts nothing is found more eminent than charity, nothing that can be given dearer than love, she holds out that love of hers which she asks for, saying,

headnotes.la: …et, et ei ex dilectione animae obediret. Finis igitur et causa creationis rerum hic est, ut Deum tota anima diligamus, illi in omnibus placeamus, ei indivisibiliter adhaereamus: juxta quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: …e end therefore and the cause of the creation of things is this, that we may love God with the whole soul, may please him in all things, may cleave to him indivisibly: according to that which is said,

headnotes.en: …d to God in that unity which Paul the Apostle sets forth to us, what can she ask of the Bridegroom which he should deny? concerning what can she intercede which he should not hear? She says therefore,

headnotes.en: I say,

headnotes.en: … cast away from his table by eternal damnation. But what is it to us to handle these matters, since these are bodily things, and this Bride of God spiritual? let her intend to inquire further, saying,

headnotes.la: …a; et est panis vitae, virtus unaquaeque perfecta: est panis vitae, corpus Christi, nobis in sacramentum et sanctificationem concessus. Hi panes sunt, quorum meminit propheta, dicens filiabus Sponsae,

headnotes.en: …d which always abides born; this is Christ Jesus our Lord; whose faith is surely conceived when the word of God, Holy Scripture, is soberly and faithfully opened and expounded. For it is written, that

headnotes.en: …criptures therefore is the first; which the Lord also reveals, when, working miracles, he deigned to refresh five thousand men with five loaves; but four thousand with seven loaves. For it is written,

headnotes.la: …de potius dilatationem et incrementa suscipiat. Pentateuchum vero, id est quinque libros Mosis, et Heptateuchum, quae sunt quatuor Evangelia, apostolorum epistolae, et Actus eorum, quos scribit Lucas,
headnotes.en: …eceives enlargement and increase. But the Pentateuch, that is, the five books of Moses, and the Heptateuch, which are the four Gospels, the epistles of the apostles, and their Acts, which Luke writes,

headnotes.la: … haec mortificamus opere, declinamus sermone, cogitatu formidamus attingere. Sic fit virtuti locus in mente; ut quod ambitio late complectitur, id pro Christo contemnatur: quod incontinentia suggerit,
headnotes.en: …side from them in speech, and dread to touch them in thought. Thus is place made for virtue in the mind; so that what ambition widely embraces, that is despised for Christ; what incontinence suggests,

headnotes.en: what is exalted through pride, that is broken by humility; and every vice that is spread abroad is driven far off by the mighty command of charity. Of this the Psalmist makes mention, saying,

headnotes.en: in which the unity of substance is shown: and when he had opened his eyes,

headnotes.la: [n: (ibid., 2)]; ecce mysterium Trinitatis. Quibus cum postea dictum sit,
headnotes.en: [n: (ibid., 2)]; behold the mystery of the Trinity. And since it was afterward said to them,

headnotes.la: ecce mysterium Unitatis
headnotes.en: behold the mystery of Unity

headnotes.la: ecce mysterium Trinitatis. Et post haec, omnia sub mysterio Trinitatis comprehenduntur, usque ad illud,
headnotes.en: behold the mystery of the Trinity. And after these things, all things are comprehended under the mystery of the Trinity, as far as that word,

headnotes.la: …lum Dei de Aegypto educendum intelligit: sicut et haec novissime, qua se Dominus praefigurans apostolis, faciem suam in modum solis, et vestimenta in candore nivis ostendit; etiam vox de coelo sonuit,
headnotes.en: …s most recent one, in which the Lord, prefiguring himself to the apostles, showed his face after the manner of the sun, and his garments in the whiteness of snow; and a voice also sounded from heaven,

headnotes.la: De hac ait haec Sponsa,
headnotes.en: Of this the Bride says,

headnotes.la: id est quae sit illa meridies,
headnotes.en: that is, what that midday may be,

headnotes.la: id est ubi quiescas, et locum tibi quietis et pausationis intimae praeparas;
headnotes.en: that is, where thou restest, and preparest for thyself a place of rest and of inmost repose;

headnotes.la: …cta Spiritu sapientiae Sponsa haec oravit ad Dominum, ut suo hanc doceret Spiritu, ubi pasceret, ubi sibi cubile in meridie eligeret. Postmodum vero paulisper elata spiritu, subjungit quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: …e Lord, that he would teach her by his Spirit where he pastured, where he chose himself a couch at midday. But afterward, being for a little while lifted up in spirit, she subjoins what has been said,

headnotes.la: …ntendere, quod nisi fiat quod postulat, ipsa se alienorum gregi immisceat. Quod attendens Dominus ipsi elatae paululum simul et paulisper iratus effertur [cn: 20 | f. *fertur*.] juxta quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: … done, she will mingle herself with the flock of strangers. Marking this, the Lord is carried a little way, and for a little while, into anger against her who was lifted up, according to what is said,

headnotes.la: Dominus enim, ut sancto sanctus, innocens innocenti, electo electus; sic justissime perverso perversus invenitur. Unde dicenti,
headnotes.en: For the Lord, as he is found holy to the holy, innocent to the innocent, elect to the elect, so most justly is he found perverse to the perverse. Whence to her saying,

headnotes.la: Respondet Dominus,
headnotes.en: The Lord answers,

headnotes.la: Attendendum vero est, quod dicitur,
headnotes.en: But it is to be marked what is said,

headnotes.la: …anorum, Judaeorum, non sequentium legem, et Christum non confitentium, Christianorum etiam, qui verbis confitentur, nosse se Deum, factis autem negant. Ut hoc ergo sibi in memoriam reducatur, dicitur,
headnotes.en: …owing the law and not confessing Christ, and of Christians also, who confess in words that they know God, but deny it by their deeds. That this therefore may be brought back to her memory, it is said,

headnotes.la: …e quidem periculum est animae perfectae, vel sponsae electae, ignorare se: hoc quidem ignorare, quod a summo Patre omnium Deo, ex nihilo creata sit, et tamen ad ejus imaginem et similitudinem formata,
headnotes.en: …en bride, to be ignorant of herself: to be ignorant, namely, of this, that she was created out of nothing by the highest Father, the God of all, and yet formed to his image and likeness. She is indeed

headnotes.la: …tum sit, quid agendum sit, quid declinandum, quod sibi fieri non vult, hoc proximo denegandum, et multa hujusmodi: quae omnia observans anima, ejus a quo creata est plene exprimit et observat imaginem
headnotes.en: … to be done to herself is to be denied to her neighbor, and many things of this kind: all which things the soul observing, fully expresses and keeps the image of him by whom it was created. But she is

headnotes.la: …arret gloriam? quam nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit, quam praeparavit Deus diligentibus se. Haec si ignorat anima aut Sponsa dilecta, quid restat nisi ut dicatur sibi,
headnotes.en: …eard, nor hath it ascended into the heart of man, which God hath prepared for them that love him. If the soul or the beloved Bride is ignorant of these things, what remains but that it be said to her,

headnotes.la: quasi a meo recede collegio,
headnotes.en: as if to say, withdraw from my company,

headnotes.la: … pasce haedos tuos? Ecce quis sibi fructus eveniet, si de bonorum collegio egressa fuerit, si male gradientes audierit, si, quod ipsi praedicant et docent, annuntiaverit. Quis fructus hic? quia pascet
headnotes.en: …have gone out from the company of the good, if she shall have listened to those who walk ill, if she shall have proclaimed what they themselves preach and teach. What fruit is this? that she will feed

headnotes.la: …ic Sponsus. Quam sibi in Sponsam elegerat, hanc commendavit verbis, delinivit obsequiis, ampliavit promissis. Quae promissa suscipiens, dum prono fertur desiderio, paulisper excessit in verbo, dicens,
headnotes.en: …Bride he commended with words, soothed with attentions, enlarged with promises. And she, receiving these promises, while she is borne along by headlong desire, went a little too far in a word, saying,

headnotes.la: …mptum fuerat, dicendo tamen aperiri fas non erat. Ad verbum hoc paulisper commotus Sponsus, unde gratiae referri debuerant, inde sibi minas intendi designans, moderate responderit, verbum irae dicens,
headnotes.en: …Bridegroom, moved for a little while at this word, marking that whence thanks ought to have been returned, thence threats were held out against him, answered with moderation, speaking a word of anger,

headnotes.la: …miscit. Quod ubi Sponso, vel interveniente Angelo, vel eo quo scit omnia modo, innotuit, virum oblitus Sponsum induit, dolenti condoluit poenitenti illico commissa remisit, memor ejus quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: … knows all things, forgetting the husband he put on the Bridegroom, he grieved with her that grieved, and to her that repented he at once forgave what she had committed, mindful of that which is said,

headnotes.la: …abstersis odiis, ira summota, ut ea quae nunc dicta sunt amoveantur a memoria, et in statum pristinum revocetur haec Sponsa, illam verbo amicabili convenit, verbo quod nondum audire promeruit, dicens,
headnotes.en: …, that the things now said might be taken away from memory and this Bride recalled to her former state, he accosts her with a word of friendship, a word which she had not yet deserved to hear, saying,

headnotes.la: sic innuens, sibi jam in te gratum esse totum quod erat a gratia imminutum. Ait ergo,
headnotes.en: thus signifying that all that had been diminished from grace is now pleasing to him in thee. He says therefore,

headnotes.la: …r, nisi qui pro Sponso fortiter ubique pugnant, et victorias ejus, coelo et aere, terra marique dilatant? Haec Angelorum illa multitudo est, quae primo cum agerentur praelia, cum dixit superba cohors,
headnotes.en: …rywhere for the Bridegroom, and spread his victories abroad in heaven and in air, by land and by sea? This is that multitude of Angels which, when battles were first waged, when the proud cohort said,

headnotes.la: …um cordibus immittente, cruci, et gladio, aliisque passionibus innumeris addicti sunt, ut horum tentationibus probarentur, et nec ipsa morte devicti, in aeterna gloria susciperentur. Ait enim Joannes,
headnotes.en: … and to the sword and to other passions innumerable, that they might be proved by the temptations of these, and, not overcome even by death itself, might be received into eternal glory. For John says,

headnotes.la: et Dominus in Job,
headnotes.en: and the Lord in Job,

headnotes.la: Hoc itaque est quod Sponsus ait,
headnotes.en: This therefore is what the Bridegroom says,

headnotes.la: …paretur; te illi meo comitatui similem constitui, sic agens pro te, sic pugnans pro te, sic eruens te, tanquam equitatui meo participem semper habere volens te. Juxta quod Judaeis a Domino dictum est,
headnotes.en: …t company of mine, so acting for thee, so fighting for thee, so rescuing thee, as one willing always to have thee a partaker of my company of horse. According to what was said by the Lord to the Jews,

headnotes.la: …rram Dei equitatus insurgeret? nec unum quidem ex reprobis superesse contingeret. Ait enim Dominus, cum eum apprehenderet profana gens, et Petrus ad hunc defendendum gladio servum Principis percuteret
headnotes.en: …ould not come about that even one of the reprobate should be left. For the Lord says, when the profane nation was seizing him, and Peter, to defend him, struck with the sword the servant of the Prince

headnotes.la: …toginta millia continet, octo minus: etiam in defensionem Elisei multa quidem millia missa sunt, quae, orante Eliseo ut aperiret Dominus oculos pueri, ipsi puero sunt demonstrata: sic enim dictum est,
headnotes.en: …d for the defence of Eliseus also many thousands indeed were sent, which, when Eliseus prayed that the Lord would open the eyes of his servant, were shown to the servant himself: for thus it was said,

headnotes.la: …st Dei, in quibus pugnat, quibus sua exercet mysteria [cn: 22 | *Ministeria*.], quibus Sponsam, quam ex hominibus elegit, assimilat, eamque sibi in decore, potestate conformat, et virtute. Ait itaque,
headnotes.en: … of God, in whom he fights, by whom he works his mysteries, to whom he likens the Bride whom he chose out of men, and conforms her to himself in comeliness, in power, and in virtue. He says therefore,

headnotes.la: id est, in praedestinatione mea, jam similem te feci,
headnotes.en: that is, in my predestination I have already made thee like

headnotes.la: Ait Sponsus ad Sponsam, ut eam deliniat, ipsamque sibi in omnibus pacatam reddat, nec ad haedos suos pascendos aliquatenus resilire permittat,
headnotes.en: The Bridegroom says to the Bride, that he may soothe her and render her at peace with him in all things, and may not allow her in any degree to spring back to the feeding of her kids,

headnotes.la: …ue iisdem reficiunt, easque in usus Ecclesiae sanctae communicando, ipsam nuptiis habilem, Deoque charam, et aeterno dignam connubio reddunt. Hi se pari junctos intelligunt Jesu Christo Domino nostro,
headnotes.en: …rting it to the uses of holy Church render her fit for the nuptials, and dear to God, and worthy of the eternal wedlock. These understand themselves to be joined as to a mate to Jesus Christ our Lord,

headnotes.la: Huic tanquam pari se jungunt, huic adhaerent, hunc diligunt; et cum in coelum jam ab eis sublatus sit,
headnotes.en: To him as to a mate they join themselves, to him they cleave, him they love; and since he has now been taken up from them into heaven, they affirm and maintain

headnotes.la: …tant, qui cito marcescunt et pereunt. Hi vero gemitum pro cantu emittunt, gementes se eo carere quod appetunt, et Dominum Jesum non apprehendere quem concupiscunt. De iis in unum collectis dictum est,
headnotes.en: …d perish. But these send forth a moan instead of a song, moaning that they lack that which they long for, and do not lay hold of the Lord Jesus whom they desire. Of these gathered into one it is said,

headnotes.la: … inventio tota, ex ipso sunt: et quibus ipsi Ecclesiam dilatant, aut magnificant, aut corroborant, divini muneris exuberatione procedunt. Quas dicit Sponsus, quia eas facturus est ipse sententias, sed
headnotes.en: …y which they enlarge, or magnify, or strengthen the Church proceed from the overflowing of the divine gift. The Bridegroom speaks of them because he himself will make them, namely those sentences, but

headnotes.la: …erunt expositores illis dare, sed et eloquii fragrantiam, unde placent, unde auditorum conviventia suscipiuntur ministrare [cn: 23 | f *auditoribus convenientia suspiciuntur ministrare*.]. Ait itaque,
headnotes.en: …rstanding which the expositors put forth, but that he also ministers the fragrance of eloquence, whereby they please, whereby they are received into the fellowship of their hearers. He says therefore,

headnotes.la: id est divinas sententias tibi conferemus
headnotes.en: that is, we will confer upon thee divine sentences,

headnotes.la: id est more vermium decoratas, et
headnotes.en: that is, adorned after the manner of worms, and set off

headnotes.la: …uod prae omnibus metallis dulcius tinnit, exornatas. Notanda vero est ipsa dicendi mutatio, quod cum hucusque Sponsus singulari sit usus eloquio, nunc eidem Sponsae verba faciens plurali numero dicit,
headnotes.en: …tals. But the very change of speech is to be marked, that whereas hitherto the Bridegroom has used the singular in his speech, now, framing his words to the same Bride, he speaks in the plural number,

headnotes.la: …et utriusque expositoribus gratiam qua id facerent, et complacerent, administravit. Unde sibi speranda est summae jam salutis redintegratio, quam, ne unquam haedis suis pascendis intendat, superius et
headnotes.en: …e whereby they might do this and be pleasing. Whence the restoring of the highest salvation is now to be hoped for by her, whom, lest she ever give heed to the feeding of her kids, he both names above

headnotes.la: …et in coelis ascensionem ad ipsum dono mirabili pertractata est. Hanc sperans pretiosam, hanc indignam repulsa reputans, hujus meminit, et illam secum permansuram aeterna stabilitate promittit dicens,
headnotes.en: …e was drawn to him by a marvellous gift. Hoping this to be precious, reckoning this unworthy of repulse, she makes mention of it, and promises that it will abide with her in eternal stability, saying,

headnotes.la: Ait itaque,
headnotes.en: He says therefore,

headnotes.la: id est, dum ille, quem regem super omnia judicio, Filius, scilicet, qui cum Patre, et Spiritu Sancto regit universa; dum ille
headnotes.en: that is, while he whom king above all things by judgment, the Son, namely, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit rules all things; while he

headnotes.la: id est in hoc mentis proposito sine labore conquiesceret,
headnotes.en: that is, was resting without labor in this purpose of his mind,

headnotes.la: …st, quem nardum, dum rex in accubitu suo esset, dedisse Sponsa protestatur. Hic odor a Patre in mundum, et in mortalium corda primo progressus est, qui indignatus serpenti quod mulierem deceperit, ait
headnotes.en: … while the king was in his repose. This odor went forth first from the Father into the world and into the hearts of mortals, who, being indignant at the serpent because he had deceived the woman, said

headnotes.la: …quos inhabitat, dum in eis dominatur, nunquam a terrenis voluptatibus et cogitationibus elevari, nunquam in lucem virtutum quae de coelo est, exsurgere, sua voluntate permittit; sed eam cunctis diebus
headnotes.en: …whom he inhabits, while he lords it in them, he never permits of his own will to be lifted from earthly pleasures and thoughts, never to rise up into the light of the virtues which is from heaven; but

headnotes.la: id est terrenis voluptatibus oblectari, in iis dormire et quiescere, tam falsa persuasione, quam falsus est ipse, compellit. Sed tandem de coelo respexit misericordia; ait enim Deus,
headnotes.en: … that is, he compels them to be delighted with earthly pleasures, to sleep and rest in them, by a persuasion as false as he himself is false. But at length mercy looked down from heaven; for God says,

headnotes.la: …romeruisse, et nolente patre Laban cum iis ad propria remeasse cognoscimus, et in extremis agentem prophetico quidem spiritu, in Juda filio suo de Christo vera prophetantem, haec dixisse non ambigimus
headnotes.en: …, to have returned with them to his own place; and, as he was at his last and prophesying by a prophetic spirit true things concerning Christ in his son Judah, we do not doubt that he said these words

headnotes.la: In quo, cum multa de passione ejus et resurrectione praedixerit, hoc quoque annectit,
headnotes.en: In which, when he had foretold many things concerning his passion and resurrection, he adds this also,

headnotes.la: Quod quidem de Christo verum est; nam a primo eorum Rege David, Reges consequenter habuerunt de tribu Judae, vel certe Duces, donec Christum apprehendentes, dicerent,
headnotes.en: Which indeed is true of Christ; for from David their first King they had Kings in succession from the tribe of Judah, or at least Leaders, until, seizing Christ, they said,

headnotes.la: [n: (Joan. XIX, 15)]
headnotes.en: [n: (Joan. XIX, 15)]

headnotes.la: adjicientes quoque dixerunt,
headnotes.en: and adding they said also,

headnotes.la: Hoc ex Christi morte consecuti sunt, de quo dicitur,
headnotes.en: This they obtained from the death of Christ, of whom it is said,

headnotes.la: vestem, scilicet, interiorem,
headnotes.en: that is, his inner garment,

headnotes.la: albo, scilicet, puro, et defaecato, clarissimo, id est interiori quadam et spirituali purificabit intelligentia
headnotes.en: white, namely, and pure and clarified, most clear, that is, he shall purify it by a certain interior and spiritual understanding

headnotes.la: vestem scilicet exteriorem, hanc mundabit,
headnotes.en: namely the outer garment, this he shall cleanse

headnotes.la: …esse est ut altiori quadam et supereminenti intelligentia praeemineant. Caeteris vero satis est, si mortem ejus et sanguinem, liberationemque suam confiteantur et credant; de quibus id praemissum est,
headnotes.en: …l by a certain higher and supereminent understanding. But for the rest it is enough if they confess and believe his death and blood and their own deliverance; concerning whom this was set down before,

headnotes.la: Christus enim vitis est, ad quem asina alligata est, id est cujus praedicatione, primitiva Judaeorum Ecclesia, quae legem utramque statuit, conversa est
headnotes.en: For Christ is the vine to which the she-ass is tied, that is, by whose preaching the primitive Church of the Jews, which established both laws, was converted. But

headnotes.la: …stum Dei virtutem et sapientiam, infirma nostra sustinentem, mortem cui erat obnoxia morte sua redimentem, credidit et adoravit. Ad hoc vero semen Moysem pertinuisse quis ambigat? qui primus scripsit,
headnotes.en: …adored Christ, the power and wisdom of God, bearing our infirmities, redeeming by his own death the death to which it was liable. But who would doubt that Moses belonged to this seed? who first wrote,

headnotes.la: Hoc enim tale est ac si dicat, Dilectus meus a me corpore elongatus est, sed a me spiritu non recessit: moram enim mecum facturus est; sed quam moram? illam de qua Dominus ait,
headnotes.en: For this is as if she should say: My Beloved has been removed far from me in body, but has not departed from me in spirit: for he will make a stay with me; but what stay? that of which the Lord says,

headnotes.la: …emper agendi quod bonum est: ut dum semper possit, semper sapiat, semper velit id quod honoris, id quod virtutis est, hinc in ea mansionem summae Trinitatis agnoscas. In Apocalypsi quoque Joannes ait,
headnotes.en: …e she can always, is always wise, always wills that which is of honor, that which is of virtue, thou mayest hence acknowledge in her the abode of the highest Trinity. In the Apocalypse also John says,

headnotes.la: … Coena dives, in qua Spiritus coelestes ministrare non dubium est; cui ille praesidet qui eorum Dominus est. In hanc quae dapes, quae fercula, quae xenia ponantur, ex hoc intellige quod ait apostolus,
headnotes.en: … it is not doubtful that the heavenly Spirits minister; over which he presides who is their Lord. What banquets, what dishes, what gifts are set out at it, understand from this which the apostle says,

headnotes.la: …sobrietas, abstinentia commendabilis, et quae circa haec sunt. Tertium locum obtinet pax, patientia, fraternus amor, et quae transcendit omnia, in Deum charitas, et contemplatio sancta. Hanc in Joanne
headnotes.en: …d the things which are about these. The third place is held by peace, patience, brotherly love, and that which transcends all, charity toward God, and holy contemplation. This the Lord in John names a

headnotes.la: …onsummari desiderat; ut hunc, timendo, poenitendo, satisfaciendo, caste vivendo, amorem ad omnes habendo, et Deum super omnia diligendo, apprehendamus, ipsoque sine fine perfruamur. Ait itaque Sponsa,
headnotes.en: …old of him by fearing, by repenting, by making satisfaction, by living chastely, by having love toward all, and by loving God above all things, and may enjoy him without end. The Bride says therefore,

headnotes.la: id est mecum,
headnotes.en: that is, with me,

headnotes.la: ac si dicat, moram facturus est. Et ut locum innuat quo moram faciet, subdit,
headnotes.en: as if she should say, he will make a stay. And that she may signify the place where he will make his stay, she adds,

headnotes.la: …netur, et hepar, et caeterae partes unde virtutes oriuntur quamplurimae, quibus corpus humanum multa ex parte regitur et vegetatur. Ut ergo locum designet ex nomine, ubi Dilectus sibi commoretur, ait,
headnotes.en: …er parts whence very many powers arise, by which the human body is in great part ruled and quickened. That therefore she may designate by name the place where the Beloved may abide with her, she says,

headnotes.la: …is actum gerit, et in se implere contendit? Implet vero temperantia, dum in iis omnibus, ne quid nimis sit, ne quid recto minus contemplatur et providet. Attendamus quid de hac Paulus asserat, dicens,
headnotes.en: …n itself? But temperance fulfils it, while in all these things it considers and provides that nothing be too much, that nothing be less than right. Let us mark what Paul asserts concerning it, saying,

headnotes.la: …e si diligenter intendat quis prosequi, hanc viam excellentiorem reperiet, id est eam cui nullis desit virtutis effectus, cui nil constet adimi quo quis ad Deum valeat propinquari. Unde ait apostolus,
headnotes.en: …ent way, that is, the way to which no effect of virtue is lacking, from which it is established that nothing is taken away whereby one might be able to be brought near to God. Whence the apostle says,

headnotes.la: …rum corpora hoc ipso consperguntur unguento, ne haec aut putredo corrumpat, aut ad haec demolienda vermis accedat: sic corpus Dominicum, myrrha legitur, et aloe fuisse perunctum. Ait ergo haec Sponsa,
headnotes.en: …prinkled with this very ointment, lest either rottenness corrupt them, or a worm come to destroy them: so the Lord's body is read to have been anointed with myrrh and aloes. This Bride says therefore,

headnotes.la: …e me et a putredine defendat, ne corrumpar; et a morsu vermium, ne demoliar: si ad arborem, planum est ex arbore fieri fasciculum, et hunc habere inter pectus ad eamdem defensionem repositum. Hic enim
headnotes.en: …rupted, and from the biting of worms, lest I be destroyed: if to the tree, it is plain that a bundle is made from a tree, and that she has this laid up within her breast for the same defence. For this

headnotes.la: Quia de Sponso loquens haec Sponsa ait,
headnotes.en: Because this Bride, speaking of the Bridegroom, says,

headnotes.la: …jus morte, cunctis eam venerantibus exhibetur. Nam sicut dolenti justum est ut dolor exhibeatur et compassio; sic mundum liberanti et redimenti vere gaudium debetur et exultatio. Unde ait haec Sponsa,
headnotes.en: …wn to all who venerate it. For as it is just that grief and compassion be shown to one who grieves, so to him who frees and redeems the world joy and exultation are truly owed. Whence this Bride says,

headnotes.la: Utrumque Paulus exprimit dicens,
headnotes.en: Paul expresses both, saying,

headnotes.la: Ecce myrrha, cui myrrham, et amaritudinem, et compassionem omnimodam debemus
headnotes.en: Behold the myrrh, to which we owe myrrh, and bitterness, and compassion of every kind

headnotes.la: De quo quidem gaudio exultans haec Sponsa, ait,
headnotes.en: Exulting indeed in this joy, this Bride says,

headnotes.la: … consitae; ex quibus, dum vulnerantur, defluit balsamum, utile quidem et pretiosum: quae quidem planities latitudinem Ecclesiae designat, quae se dignoscitur in quatuor jam mundi partes dilatare. Haec
headnotes.en: …ounded, there flows down balsam, useful indeed and precious: which plain indeed signifies the breadth of the Church, which is known to spread itself now into the four parts of the world. This is named

headnotes.la: nominata est, quod est,
headnotes.en: which is,

headnotes.la: …cclesiae, in quo dum haedi purgantur, ex haedis agni efficiuntur. Virtus in his Christi patet, ubi ex arbore vulnerata fluit balsamum, sicut ex Christo vulnerato fluxit benedictionis oleum, dum dixit,
headnotes.en: …e cleansed, out of kids lambs are made. The power of Christ appears in these things, where from the wounded tree flows balsam, just as from the wounded Christ flowed the oil of blessing, when he said,

headnotes.la: …radens homini propitiatur Deus; hoc denuo consecrantur Reges, inunguntur Pontifices, ordinantur sacerdotes, Christo sua dona pro populo offerentes, et ei sua reddentes. Hoc itaque est quod ait Sponsa,
headnotes.en: …this again kings are consecrated, bishops anointed, priests ordained, offering to Christ his own gifts on behalf of the people, and rendering to him what is his. This therefore is what the Bride says,

headnotes.la: quod patet in
headnotes.en: which appears in

headnotes.la: Quo in loco id attendendum est, quod Sponsam suam Sponsus triplici jam magnificavit elogio. dicens,
headnotes.en: In which place this is to be observed, that the Bridegroom has already magnified his Bride with a threefold commendation. saying,

headnotes.la: et illo,
headnotes.en: and that other,

headnotes.la: tertium quoque adjiciens,
headnotes.en: adding also a third,

headnotes.la: Cui Sponsa quoque trina laude respondet, dicens,
headnotes.en: To whom the Bride also answers with a threefold praise, saying,

headnotes.la: et illo,
headnotes.en: and that other,

headnotes.la: et quod sequitur,
headnotes.en: and that which follows,
