headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *nihil mihi prodest*, "it profiteth me nothing"] The same also says,

headnotes.la: …ue cervorum similis, qui stat post parietem, per fenestras cancellosque conspiciens, quid intus agatur, quod placeat, vel quod sibi displiceat. Nunc vero, quod sibi Sponsus loquatur, insinuat, dicens,
headnotes.en: …standeth behind the wall, beholding through the windows and the lattices what is done within, what pleases him, or what displeases him. But now she intimates that the Bridegroom speaks to her, saying,

headnotes.la: Quam tribus hortatur verbis, dicens
headnotes.en: Whom he exhorts with three words, saying

headnotes.la: tribus hanc designat nominibus, dicens,
headnotes.en: and whom he designates with three names, saying,

headnotes.la: ut amica nominum positio totum leviget, quod verborum fieri urget trina praeceptio. Ait enim,
headnotes.en: that the friendly setting of the names may lighten all that the threefold command of the words urges to be done. For he says,

headnotes.la: nam ex hoc cognovi te amantem me, quod reliquisti patrem et matrem, fratres et sorores, domum et agros, et secuta es me. Te etiam in Paulo dicentem audivi,
headnotes.en: for from this I knew thee loving me, that thou hast left father and mother, brothers and sisters, house and fields, and hast followed me. Thee also have I heard saying in Paul,

headnotes.la: Te etiam in Petro protestantem audivi,
headnotes.en: Thee also have I heard protesting in Peter,

headnotes.la: Addit quoque,
headnotes.en: He adds also,

headnotes.la: …idem columbae, quae Christo protestata est in baptismate, similem, quantum potes conformans, et mihi in ejusmodi forma complacens; tu quam juste formosam rationibus istis approbo, Surge. Dicens autem,
headnotes.en: … as thou canst to the likeness of that dove which bore witness to Christ in his baptism, and pleasing me in such a form; thou whom by these reasons I justly approve as beautiful, Arise. But in saying,

headnotes.la: non eo modo protulit, quo peccatori dicitur, Surge. Peccatori namque dicitur,
headnotes.en: he did not utter it in that manner in which it is said to a sinner, Arise. For to a sinner it is said,

headnotes.la: … est, a peccatis quiescat; et exsurgat a mortuis, id est ne in inferno, inter mortuos sibi locum manendi constituat: et cum peccare desieris, et haec, quae tibi placebant jam abhorrere inceperis, tunc
headnotes.en: …rom the dead, that is, that he set not for himself a place of abiding in hell, among the dead: and when thou shalt have ceased to sin, and hast begun now to abhor these things which pleased thee, then

headnotes.la: … ire te velit, ostendet. Nec hoc modo quidem hic Sponsae dicitur, ut surgat, quae jamdiu patrem et matrem, domum et fratres, et caetera quae in mundo habentur, reliquerat, et Christum secuta, dixerat,
headnotes.en: …s way said here to the Bride that she arise, who long since had left father and mother, house and brothers, and the rest of the things that are had in the world, and, having followed Christ, had said,

headnotes.la: …e resurgere, ipsumque dehinc ad coelos ascendere, et sequentibus se bona coelestia promisisse, constabat, toto amplecteretur desiderio, optaret voto, jucundaretur soliloquio: huic igitur Dilectus ait,
headnotes.en: …he heavens, and to have promised heavenly goods to those that follow him, she embraced with her whole desire, longed for with a vow, and delighted in with soliloquy: to her therefore the Beloved says,

headnotes.la: quod est, Excitare ab hac quiete tua, ab hac pace tua: Ego quidem sum, qui adjurans filias Jerusalem, dixi,
headnotes.en: which is, Rouse thyself from this rest of thine, from this peace of thine: I indeed am he who, adjuring the daughters of Jerusalem, said,

headnotes.la: …oedo permisceri concubitu, luxus, et quae luxum comitatur importunitas imperabat. Testatur hoc Adae primi patris inobedientia; testatur et Caini malitia; testatur et Lamech [cn: 37 | f. *homicidium.*]
headnotes.en: …ty that accompanies luxury, commanded that all things be mingled in foul intercourse. This the disobedience of Adam the first father bears witness to; the malice of Cain also bears witness; and Lamech

headnotes.la: … eversi sunt, quia Scriptura sancta viluit, quae nobis ad Deum pontem facit. Commeatus viatori non patuit, quia ab hac vita egredienti nullus ad Deum accessus exstitit. Facta enim est, ut ait Dominus,
headnotes.en: …re, which makes for us a bridge to God, became cheap. No passage lay open to the traveller, because for him going forth from this life there was no access to God. For there was made, as the Lord says,

headnotes.la: … in aeternum futura communio. Te itaque, quam amicam sentio, quia vis quod volo; te, quam columbinis praestantem moribus intelligo, quam mihi conformem, ideoque formosam judico, te evoco, tibi dicens,
headnotes.en: …eive to be my friend, because thou willest what I will; thee, whom I understand to excel in dove-like manners, whom I judge conformed to me, and therefore beautiful, thee I call forth, saying to thee,

headnotes.la: …oc est, Ab hac contemplatione pacis et quietis qua detineris, egredere; propera, ut meae praeceptionis imperium tuae sub dicto [cn: 39 | f. *subito*, vel, *cum dicto.*] sequatur obeditionis obsequium,
headnotes.en: that is, Come forth from this contemplation of peace and quiet wherein thou art held; make haste, that the compliance of thy obedience may follow at a word upon the command of my precept,

headnotes.la: … sunt, cantu suo hiemis abcessum, et veris nuntians adventum, gemit hic, pudicitiam amans in altis habitat, fugit hominum conversationem, corpore in mundo, mente in coelo permanens: unde Baptista ait,
headnotes.en: …re of winter and the coming of spring; he moans here, and, loving chastity, he dwells on high, he flees the converse of men, remaining in body in the world, in mind in heaven: whence the Baptist says,

headnotes.la: Petrus vero ait
headnotes.en: But Peter says

headnotes.la: Paulus quoque ait
headnotes.en: Paul also says

headnotes.la: …imitivus fructus abundanter nascitur, quia tunc quod in ficu est amaritudinis pene emittitur, spes bona sequentis est, ut quo iste amarior, eo sequens ille dulcior emittatur. De hac ergo ficu dicitur,
headnotes.en: …erness that is in the fig is sent forth, there is good hope of that which follows, that the more bitter this one is, the sweeter that which follows may be sent forth. Of this fig therefore it is said,

headnotes.la: Haec enim ficus est de qua dicitur in Evangelio: Arborem ficum habebat quidam plantatam in vinea sua, in qua, tribus annis veniens dominus, et in ea fructum non inveniens, ait cultori
headnotes.en: … this is the fig tree of which it is said in the Gospel: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, to which the lord coming for three years, and finding no fruit on it, said to the dresser

headnotes.la: de qua cultor ait
headnotes.en: of which the dresser said

headnotes.la: …, scilicet, anno, eo quidem tempore quod ante legem exstitit; altero, scilicet, quod sub lege fuit; tertio quidem, quod sub gratia incepit) fructus quidem non invenit; unde iratus haec verba protulit,
headnotes.en: …at time which was before the law; in the second, namely, that which was under the law; in the third indeed, that which began under grace) found no fruit; whence, being angered, he uttered these words,

headnotes.la: …la reputaretur. Nam toto hoc tempore, si quos justos reperis, caeteraeque multitudini compares, sic erit comparatio, quasi modicum quid infinitae compares multitudini, unde salvator Dominus noster ait
headnotes.en: …hou find any just men, and compare them with the rest of the multitude, the comparison will be as if thou shouldst compare some small thing with an infinite multitude; whence our Lord and Saviour says

headnotes.la: … dilecturi sunt: haec quidem una est, in unitate fidei, et spei, et charitatis permanens: quae quidem tunc apparebit, cum Dominus orbem terrae judicabit, qui regnum a Domino percipient, dicente Domino
headnotes.en: … one, abiding in the unity of faith, and of hope, and of charity: which indeed shall then appear, when the Lord shall judge the world, they who shall receive the kingdom from the Lord, the Lord saying

headnotes.la: qui jam tunc erunt liberi a
headnotes.en: who then shall already be free from the

headnotes.la: … spirituum, quam miseris tendunt mortalibus, ut eos peccatis illaqueent, et illaqueatos ad mortem deducant: verbum vero asperum (quo nihil in mundo asperius esse potest), illud est quod audituri sunt,
headnotes.en: …stretch out for wretched mortals, that they may ensnare them in sins, and lead the ensnared to death: but the sharp word (than which nothing in the world can be sharper) is that which they shall hear,

headnotes.la: Evocavit jam Dilectus Sponsam, ut veniret ad se: eam quoque septem his propositis invitavit, dicens,
headnotes.en: The Beloved has now called forth the Bride, that she might come to him: he has invited her also by these seven things set forth, saying,

headnotes.la: Quibus omnibus, temporis opportunitas ostensa est ut veniret. Adhuc quoque in eadem perseverans vocatione ad ipsum, repetit dicens,
headnotes.en: By all which the opportuneness of the time was shown, that she should come. And still persevering in the same calling of her to himself, he repeats, saying,

headnotes.la: Addit quoque,
headnotes.en: He adds also,

headnotes.la: Quae quidem verba memoriam Dominicae passionis adjiciunt. Quis enim ignoret, de Christo dixisse apostolum,
headnotes.en: Which words indeed add the memory of the Lord's passion. For who is ignorant that the apostle said of Christ,

headnotes.la: … petra foramina esse, quis nesciat, qui Christum clavis affixum cruci fuisse non dubitat? In hac etiam maceriae cavernam inesse, quis nesciat, qui quod legit verum esse non dubitet? Scriptum est enim,
headnotes.en: …d not know, who doubts not that Christ was fastened to the cross with nails? That there is also a hollow in this wall, who would not know, who doubts not that what he reads is true? For it is written,

headnotes.la: Obedit Sponsa Dilecto suo; nescit moram cum vocatur. Sic enim ei dictum est,
headnotes.en: The Bride obeys her Beloved; she knows no delay when she is called. For thus it was said to her,

headnotes.la: …roperans venit, mora non interveniente assistit. Venit autem operto capite, ne faciem ejus sol exurat, ne candor ejus solis candore degeneret. Assistenti autem Dilectae, et operienti se, dilectus ait,
headnotes.en: …ning. But she comes with her head covered, lest the sun burn her face, lest her whiteness be made base by the whiteness of the sun. But to the Bride standing by and covering herself, the Beloved says,

headnotes.la: Sponsam enim Dilecto suo revelata facie praesentari, justum est. Nam si Rebecca, ad puteum, cujus nomen,
headnotes.en: For it is just that the Bride be presented to her Beloved with unveiled face. For if Rebecca, at the well whose name is

headnotes.la: et,
headnotes.en: and

headnotes.la: …cto suo jamdiu dilecta, Sponso jamdiu desponsata, et amore spirituali et soliloquiis divinis jam cognita, non opus est ut coram Sponso operta appareat, sed revelata facie ipsum contempletur et diligat
headnotes.en: …the Bridegroom, and now known by spiritual love and by divine soliloquies, there is no need that she should appear veiled before the Bridegroom, but with unveiled face let her contemplate and love him

headnotes.la: …sui usque ad exitus sui finem speculetur et consideret; quaeque sunt cogitationis, et locutionis, et antiquae consuetudinis et operationis, ipse sibi recte denuntiet? Unde in psalmo ter ipse David ait
headnotes.en: … beginning even to the end of its issue; and rightly declare to himself whatever belongs to thought, and to speech, and to ancient habit and to work? Whence in the psalm David himself says three times

headnotes.la: et item
headnotes.en: and again

headnotes.la: tertioque subjungit
headnotes.en: and a third time he subjoins

headnotes.la: … homini, ut ab iis convertatur quae in cogitatu deliquit; ut convertatur ab eis quae deliquit in verbo; et ab iis quae in opere deliquit et consuetudine; unde post trinam hanc invocationem, subjungit,
headnotes.en: …s offended in thought; that he be converted from those wherein he has offended in word; and from those wherein he has offended in deed and in habit; whence after this threefold invocation he subjoins,

headnotes.la: …lut evaserit. Sic quoque revelata facie Deus nos videre desiderat, ut nil in nobis se indignum in cogitatu appareat, nil prorsus in verbo quod offendat, nil in actu et opere quod displiceat. Unde ait,
headnotes.en: … God desires to see us with unveiled face, that nothing in us may appear in thought unworthy of him, nothing at all in word that may offend, nothing in act and deed that may displease. Whence he says,

headnotes.la: …ta jam facies, ubi nil quod reprehendatur intervenit, datur ulterius progrediendi licentia; ut sicut de facie Dilecti ejus delectatur aspectus, sic sono vocis ejusdem delectetur auditus: unde dicitur,
headnotes.en: …reprehended, licence is given of advancing further; that as the sight is delighted by the face of her Beloved, so the hearing may be delighted by the sound of the voice of the same: whence it is said,

headnotes.la: …uo attendendum est, voces nostras diversis modis in aure sonare Domini. Sonamus enim quandoque sono Deo tantum audibili, cum ad ipsum cordis tantum devotione loquimur; sicut de Anna scriptum est, quod
headnotes.en: …r voices sound in the ear of the Lord in divers ways. For sometimes we sound with a sound audible to God alone, when we speak to him with the devotion of the heart only; as it is written of Anna, that

headnotes.la: …versae voces et innumerae, quas in Dei laudem humana promit inventio; quas, nimirum, debita si comitetur devotio, Dei auribus insonare et postulata suscipere, dubium non est. Hinc etiam propheta dicit
headnotes.en: …nvention puts forth unto the praise of God; which, assuredly, if due devotion accompany them, there is no doubt that they sound in the ears of God and obtain what is asked. Hence also the prophet says

headnotes.la: Et operis fine, ultimo concludit psalmo
headnotes.en: And at the end of the work, he concludes with the last psalm

headnotes.la: Ubi decem vicibus ad laudem monens coelestium novem ordines, hominemque eis adjunctum, et parem eis per gratiam factam, ad laudem invitat, dicens,
headnotes.en: Where, admonishing unto praise ten times over, he invites to praise the nine orders of the heavenly ones, and man joined to them and made equal to them through grace, saying,

headnotes.la: quae me solum confitetur et orat, magnificat et glorificat, mihi de commissis supplicandum aestimat, et post concessam veniam, dari sibi gratiam exoptat et gloriam
headnotes.en: …ses and prays to me alone, magnifies and glorifies, judges that supplication is to be made to me for the things she has committed, and, after pardon granted, longs that grace and glory be given to her

headnotes.la: …ram ignoravit haec Sponsa, a Dilecto suo properans ut ad se veniret, evocata, statim surrexit, majestati statim astitit; et quia, ne opprimeretur a gloria, operta venit, audire meruit quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: …that she should come to him, she straightway arose, straightway stood before his majesty; and because she came covered, lest she should be overwhelmed by the glory, she deserved to hear what was said,

headnotes.la: quod est, revelata me facie contemplare;
headnotes.en: which is, With face unveiled, contemplate me;

headnotes.la: id est, pete quod vis, quam scio nil petituram nisi justa. A Sponso suscepta, meretur intelligere et videre quod promissum est, scilicet, quod
headnotes.en: that is, Ask what thou wilt, thou of whom I know that she will ask nothing but what is just. Received by the Bridegroom, she deserves to understand and to see what was promised, namely, that

headnotes.la: …ne cum illa possederit, ex toto rudis existat. Quod quia sibi agendum est, et in honorem Dilectae suae quodammodo vacandum, admonet sodales suos, ut interim vineas custodiant quae effloruerunt jam, et
headnotes.en: …ecause this is to be done by him, and he must in a manner be at leisure for the honour of his Beloved, he admonishes his companions that meanwhile they guard the vineyards which have now flowered, and

headnotes.la: ne vulpes eas demoliantur, et labores iis exhibiti ad inane redigantur: hortatur autem sic,
headnotes.en: lest the foxes destroy them, and the labours bestowed on them be brought to nothing: and he exhorts thus,

headnotes.la: Loquitur autem ad sodales suos, id est, ad administratorios spiritus; de quibus Paulus ait,
headnotes.en: But he speaks to his companions, that is, to the ministering spirits; of whom Paul says,

headnotes.la: …t quod inceperant; sed haec omnia in bonum illis cooperari cernentes, posse suum nihil esse conspicerent, nisi quatenus a Deo permitterentur. Bonis igitur angelis id mandatur a Domino quod dictum est,
headnotes.en: …ether unto good for them, they might perceive that their own power was nothing, save in so far as they were permitted by God. To the good angels therefore that is commanded by the Lord which was said,

headnotes.la: …lpes errare, omnesque dolo perturbare conspicitis, hos capite, hos impedite, nilque eos posse, nisi quod meae placitum est voluntati, perficite. Harum vero vulpium Dominus in Evangelio meminit, dicens
headnotes.en: …isturbing all men by guile, catch these, hinder these, and bring it to pass that they can do nothing except what is pleasing to my will. But the Lord makes mention of these foxes in the Gospel, saying

headnotes.la: Dicenti enim sibi,
headnotes.en: For to him who said to him,

headnotes.la: Salvator ait,
headnotes.en: the Saviour says,

headnotes.la: …at, Non te suscipio, non te mihi praedestinatum, sed vulpibus datum intelligo, ut vulpes te lacerent, et volucres coeli, qui sunt spiritus maligni, diripiant te. Idem quoque de Herode minante sibi ait
headnotes.en: …ot to be predestined to me, but given to the foxes, that the foxes may tear thee, and the birds of the air, who are the malignant spirits, may rend thee. The same also he says of Herod threatening him

headnotes.la: …morbo gravati sunt, sanitatem perficio; et tunc die tertia consummabor, id est, tunc moriar, et consummata erunt omnia quae potest inimicus homo in me. Harum etiam vulpium meminit David, dicens Domino
headnotes.en: …ird day I shall be consummated, that is, then I shall die, and all things shall be consummated which the enemy man is able to do against me. Of these foxes also David makes mention, saying to the Lord

headnotes.la: Qui enim Dominum occiderunt, animam ejus perdere quaesierunt, sed in vanum, quia vivit: ecce Dominus Rex in aeternum
headnotes.en: For they who slew the Lord sought to destroy his soul, but in vain, because he lives: behold the Lord is King for ever

headnotes.la: …scentiam, et allocutionem, titillatione mala excrescente, actus male desideratus impletur, et castitas diu impugnata dejicitur. Sic quoque alitur et nutritur visione cupiditas, dum se non metitur homo
headnotes.en: …erse, as the evil titillation grows, the act evilly desired is fulfilled, and chastity long assailed is cast down. So also covetousness is fed and nourished by sight, while a man measures not himself,

headnotes.la: …non ignorat. Sic infinitum hoc malitiae dedecus, cum numeri multiplicatione contendit, nunquam sibi ponens modum, cum aliquem invenerit, in quem possit excrescere, numerum ampliorem. Unde Salvator ait
headnotes.en: …is boundless disgrace of malice strives with the multiplication of number, never setting a measure to itself, so long as it has found some larger number into which it may grow. Whence the Saviour says

headnotes.la: Et iterum
headnotes.en: And again

headnotes.la: … eos ab ore et faucibus imis Satanae eripit, et ad coelestia regna perducit. Sic caeterae virtutes emolliuntur, sic pereunt, vitium sic possidet quod arte maligni comprehensum est. Unde recte dicitur,
headnotes.en: …ads them through to the heavenly kingdoms. So are the other virtues softened, so do they perish, so does vice possess what has been seized by the craft of the malignant one. Whence it is rightly said,

headnotes.la: quod est, vulpibus his resistite dum sunt parvulae, primos earum motus concutite, ne valeant excrescere, ad me, qui sum petra firmissima, collidite
headnotes.en: which is, Resist these foxes while they are little, shake their first motions, lest they be able to grow, dash them against me, who am the most firm rock

headnotes.la: … venit; cum qua Dominus miscet colloquia, miscet (ut sic dicam) soliloquia; soli enim Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui sancto, nota sunt haec quae dicuntur, quae Sponsae huic revelantur: unde et ipsa ait,
headnotes.en: …at I may so speak) soliloquies; for to the Father alone, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, are these things known which are spoken, which are revealed to this Bride: whence she herself also says,

headnotes.la: quasi alloquitur;
headnotes.en: as though he speaks to me;

headnotes.la: …citurnitati commendatis, quae soli Sponsae loquitur Deus, annectit Sponsa, quid in supernis agat Sponsus, quo jucundetur, quo oblectetur, quo reficiatur, quae illi pastio magis grata habeatur, dicens,
headnotes.en: …o the Bride alone, the Bride adds what the Bridegroom does in the heights, wherein he is gladdened, wherein he is delighted, wherein he is refreshed, what pasture is held more pleasing to him, saying,

headnotes.la: …existant, nil mundi hujus sibi vindicantes, ut eos non inflammet libido, non stimulet avaritia, non effeminet lascivia, non sternat ambitio, invidia non maceret, non secularis cura negotii sollicitet,
headnotes.en: …them, that avarice may not goad them, that wantonness may not unman them, that ambition may not lay them low, that envy may not waste them, that the secular care of business may not make them anxious,

headnotes.la: Dictum est, quod inter lilia Dilectus pascitur, nunc vero dicendum est, quamdiu inter eadem, aliis non adjunctis sibi ad pascendum commorabitur; hoc enim est quod dicitur,
headnotes.en: It has been said that the Beloved is fed among the lilies; but now it must be said how long he will abide among the same, others not being joined to him for the feeding; for this is what is said,

headnotes.la: …eipsum ostendet, reddens unicuique juxta opera sua; bonis sine fine bona, malis mala quidem sine fine permansura. Dies quidem Domini recte duo nominantur: unus, quo judicatus est, et de eo dictum est,
headnotes.en: … to the good, good things without end, to the evil, evil things indeed that shall abide without end. Two days indeed of the Lord are rightly named: one, in which he was judged, and of him it was said,

headnotes.la: itemque de eo dictum est, ut
headnotes.en: and likewise of him it was said, that

headnotes.la: Alter, quo totum a morte suscitatum judicabit orbem terrarum,
headnotes.en: The other, in which he shall judge the whole world raised up from death,

headnotes.la: dies quo
headnotes.en: the day in which

headnotes.la: Evocata jamdiu Sponsa vocanti se Sponso astitit, ipsum inter lilia coelestia pascentem vidit, id ipsum exoptans sibi suisque audire meruit ut expectet,
headnotes.en: …since called forth, stood by the Bridegroom who called her, saw him feeding among the heavenly lilies, and, longing for that very thing for herself and for hers, deserved to hear that she should wait,

headnotes.la: …rris exorta lilia congregabuntur, et supernis aggregata et assimilata liliis, hoc quidem dono munerabuntur, ut inter ipsa pascatur Sponsus, et in aeternum delectetur, et ipsa illud decantent apostoli,
headnotes.en: …ed and made like to the lilies above, shall be endowed with this gift, that the Bridegroom may be fed among them, and be delighted for ever, and that they themselves may sing that word of the apostle,

headnotes.la: … justus judex. Unde supplex orat, ut revertatur Sponsus, et visitet, et foveat Ecclesiam quae terris laborat; ut labores ejus ipse suscipiat, ipse provehat, et ipse ad perfectum usque perducat, dicens
headnotes.en: …room may return, and visit, and cherish the Church which labours on the earth; that he himself may take up her labours, himself advance them, and himself lead them through even unto perfection, saying

headnotes.la: Sequitur,
headnotes.en: There follows,

headnotes.la: …senta, hanc in ejus memoria revoca, ut te laudet, te adoret, te glorificet super omnes montes Bether, nullum tibi in Ecclesia aequalem reputans, sed te super omnes montes qui sunt in Bether, quod est,
headnotes.en: …hee above all the mountains of Bether, reckoning none equal to thee in the Church, but understanding thee to be far more sublime and far more holy than all the mountains which are in Bether, which is,

headnotes.la: vel,
headnotes.en: or,

headnotes.la: vel,
headnotes.en: or,

headnotes.la: …am tamen laborantem in terris respiciat, ejusque labori miseratus condescendat; jam nunc, ut eum facilius pietas moveat, et ad ea quae rogantur inclinari faciat, ipsius annectit verba quibus supplicat
headnotes.en: …ity, condescend to her labour; now already, that mercy may the more easily move him, and make him to be inclined to the things which are asked, she adds the words of the same wherewith she supplicates

headnotes.la: Attendendum vero hoc loco est, quod Salomon rex festivus, et in rebus omnibus opulentus, deliciis quoque deditus (ut mos plerisque regibus est), hanc suam mundo notificet opulentiam, scribens ait
headnotes.en: …be noted in this place, that Solomon, a festive king, and opulent in all things, given also to delights (as is the custom with most kings), makes known this his opulence to the world, and writing says

headnotes.la: … Rex enim iste festivus Salomon, magnus ille Rex est, qui est Pater, qui est Filius, qui et Spiritus sanctus est, qui unam, dum currunt secula tribus ordinibus, sibi jungit Ecclesiam; cujus eam partem
headnotes.en: … is that great King, who is the Father, who is the Son, who is also the Holy Ghost, who, while the ages run their course, joins to himself one Church in three orders; of which he designates that part,

headnotes.la: …ularum designat nominatione. Et quidem reginarum designantur ex nomine, quae jamdiu concurrerunt, quae post trahentem ascenderunt, et trahentem hunc comprehendere meruerunt; sic ut cum Apostolo dicant
headnotes.en: …ey are designated by the name of queens who have long since run together, who have ascended after him that draws, and have deserved to lay hold of him that draws; so that with the Apostle they may say

headnotes.en: …groom, roused from sleep after the delay, knowing that she had gone away and was anxious for him, does that which belongs to a lover: he follows her, and finding the door shut, he knocks at it, saying

headnotes.la: ac si dicat, Venientem ad te me suscipe; habitaculum quaerenti in te, non me respuas; sed oris ostium, cordis habitaculum in te mihi studeas aperire, qui te solam quaerens desidero invenire, quae
headnotes.en: … to thee; reject me not, who seek a dwelling in thee; but be earnest to open to me the door of thy mouth, the dwelling of thy heart within thee, I who, seeking thee alone, desire to find thee, who art

headnotes.la: Causam cur sibi Sponsus aperiri postulat, his verbis ostendit, dicens
headnotes.en: The cause why the Bridegroom asks that it be opened to him, he shows by these words, saying

headnotes.la: …iose diffunditur. Volens igitur Sponsus, Sponsam suam hoc rore perfundi, volens, ipsam his guttis, quae de nocte, id est, citra conscientiam hominum formantur, adimpleri, sibi postulat aperiri, dicens
headnotes.en: …g that his Bride be steeped in this dew, willing that she herself be filled with these drops, which are formed by night, that is, apart from the knowledge of men, asks that it be opened to him, saying

headnotes.la: causamque subjiciens, ait
headnotes.en: and adding the cause, he says

headnotes.la: …ut meum plenum est rore. Caput enim Christi Deus est, cui omnis plenitudo sapientiae et scientiae inesse dignoscitur, quem, qui Christum suscipiunt, in se quidem habere, et ejus dona, cognoscuntur; et
headnotes.en: … of dew. For the head of Christ is God, in whom all the fulness of wisdom and knowledge is known to dwell, whom they that receive Christ are known to have in themselves indeed, and his gifts also; and

headnotes.la: …m pulsantis Sponsi, et ad se ingredi cupientis, rore quem inferre cupit Sponsus, guttisque noctium nondum intellectis, expavescit, et non respondens Sponso, sibi loquitur, sibique verba facit, dicens,
headnotes.en: … the Bridegroom desires to bring in, and the drops of the nights, being not yet understood, is affrighted, and, not answering the Bridegroom, speaks to herself, and makes her words to herself, saying,

headnotes.la: Putans enim, se ad conversationem pristinam et antiquam revocari, et ob necessitatem proximi mundanis hisce negotiis implicari timens, et conquerens, nec tamen Sponso respondens, sibi ait,
headnotes.en: …ck to her former and ancient manner of life, and fearing to be entangled in these worldly affairs for her neighbour's necessity, and complaining, yet not answering the Bridegroom, she says to herself,

headnotes.la: …t, conversatione antiqua privata sum, et ad Christum in baptismate conversa sum, huic bonorum praedicatione connexa sum: illam quonam modo jam induam? in quonam modo complectar quod nesciam? unde ait,
headnotes.en: …ve been converted to Christ in baptism, and have been knit to him by the preaching of good men: in what manner shall I now put that on? in what manner shall I embrace what I know not? whence she says,

headnotes.la: Ejus quidem pedes, affectiones suae sunt, quas lavit credendo, exhortationibus sanctorum acquiescendo, Paulum audiendo, qui ait,
headnotes.en: Her feet indeed are her affections, which she washed by believing, by acquiescing in the exhortations of the saints, by hearing Paul, who says,

headnotes.la: Excusatione apud se reverenter praemissa, nec tamen Sponso responsione facta, quid sibi dilectus fecerit, consequenter ostendit, dicens
headnotes.en: Her excuse having been reverently made beforehand within herself, yet no answer having been made to the Bridegroom, she next shows what her beloved had done for her, saying

headnotes.la: Unde beatus Gregorius sic ait,
headnotes.en: Whence blessed Gregory thus says,

headnotes.la: Haec secreta visitationis supernae senserat ille, qui ait,
headnotes.en: These secrets of the heavenly visitation he had felt who says,

headnotes.la: et beatus Paulus dicens,
headnotes.en: and blessed Paul, saying,

headnotes.la: …s hinc ait, foramen nostrum, id est, quo videmus opera Christi, oculus, scilicet, mentis, per quem Christus intrat, quo ipsum Deum esse vere cognoscimus, quo ipsi cum Propheta jucundissime decantamus,
headnotes.en: …at is, that whereby we see the works of Christ, namely, the eye of the mind, through which Christ enters, whereby we truly know him to be God, whereby we ourselves most joyfully sing with the Prophet,

headnotes.la: Itemque illud,
headnotes.en: And likewise that,

headnotes.la: … solo, quo cuncta creata sunt et manent in aeternum. Quae videns mundus, et admirans testimonia, vera esse perhibuit; quae si falsa forent, nullum perciperent ex falsitate virtutis effectum. Unde ait,
headnotes.en: …ide for ever. Which things the world seeing, and marvelling at the testimonies, declared them to be true; and if they were false, they would receive from falsehood no effect of power. Whence she says,

headnotes.la: … divinis non obsistens operibus, tota contremit, Deum factum hominem expavescit; quae tamen desuper data sunt, haec ore cognoscit, corde diligit, et donis Spiritus sancti attacta, contremiscendo, ait,
headnotes.en: … has been made man; yet the things which have been given from above, these it acknowledges with the mouth, loves with the heart, and, being touched by the gifts of the Holy Spirit, trembling, it says,

headnotes.la: id est, a me peccatorum onus quo aggravabar excussi. Unde dictum est,
headnotes.en: that is, I shook off from me the burden of sins wherewith I was weighed down. Whence it is said,

headnotes.la: …ilias, et caetera hujusmodi, caro a luxuriae illecebris revocatur, et beato continentiae fine decoratur: hanc se suis manibus stillasse, id est, in cunctis suis operibus demonstrasse perhibet, dicens,
headnotes.en: …back from the allurements of luxury, and is adorned with the blessed end of continence: she declares that she has dropped this with her own hands, that is, has shown it forth in all her works, saying,

headnotes.la: Ideoque
headnotes.en: And therefore she adds

headnotes.la: Quo in loco virtutem
headnotes.en: In which place she opens the virtue of

headnotes.la: …os enim, discretio demonstratur: quia [cn: 61 | F. *quod*.] post digiti tactu tangitur, id certa quadam ratione mentis intelligitur. Unde ne ad hanc castitatis custodiam modus excedatur, adjectum est,
headnotes.en: … because after it is touched by the touch of the finger, that is understood by a certain sure reasoning of the mind. Whence, lest in this guardianship of chastity the measure be exceeded, it is added,

headnotes.la: Ne solum in castitatis continentia accessus ad dilectum demonstretur, hoc adjicitur
headnotes.en: Lest the approach to the beloved should be shown to lie in the continence of chastity alone, this is added

headnotes.la: …, ac aptasse manus, id est, opera, ut praedicaret; hanc continentiam cunctis monuisse, ut sic Sponso accederent, sicque possulum ostii amovisse, ut Christo cuncti cohaererent, et ipsum sic possiderent
headnotes.en: …at she might preach; that she admonished all to continence, that so they might approach the Bridegroom, and thus removed the *possulum* of the door, that all might cleave to Christ, and so possess him

headnotes.la: ne apprehensus teneretur;
headnotes.en: lest, being laid hold on, he should be held;

headnotes.la: …tus haec sunt. Ut ad ignem cera, ad solem candida nix liquescit, sic ad adventum Sponsi sui haec Sponsa liquefacta est, et a sua, quam jam in se pigritia et duritia collegerat, immutata. Sic enim ait,
headnotes.en: …he fire, and white snow at the sun, so at the coming of her Bridegroom this Bride was melted, and was changed from that sloth and hardness which she had already gathered in herself. For thus she says,

headnotes.la: …deplorat incommoda, vel commissa, cum statum plangit hujus miseriae, cui ex necessitate subjicitur, sic cum dilationem plangit futurae gloriae, ad quam non ex voto suscipitur, liquitur quidem, dicens,
headnotes.en: …tate of this misery, to which she is subjected of necessity, thus when she bewails the delay of the glory to come, into which she is not received according to her desire, she is indeed melted, saying,

headnotes.la: … animam, omnes qui ab Adam usque in finem, nasciturum, vel natum ex Virgine Christum, Dei Filium, mundumque morte sua redempturum, crediderint; quas omnes, ob unitatem fidei, velut unam nominans, ait,
headnotes.en: …ve believed that Christ, the Son of God, was to be born, or was born, of the Virgin, and would redeem the world by his death; all of whom, for the unity of faith, naming them as it were one, she says,

headnotes.la: Subdit vero,
headnotes.en: But she subjoins,

headnotes.la: Quod ut diligentius attendatur, illud beati Pauli considerandum est; ait enim,
headnotes.en: That this may be the more diligently considered, that saying of blessed Paul is to be weighed; for he says,

headnotes.la: Hic quidem in prophetis
headnotes.en: Here indeed he spoke

headnotes.la: …agna enim multiplicitas sententiarum, quas per eos Dominus locutus est, non poterat paucis explicari: contracta namque brevitas obscuritatem gignit, quae nimirum obscuritas intelligentiam non admittit
headnotes.en: …great manifoldness of the sentences which the Lord spoke through them could not be unfolded in few: for a contracted brevity begets obscurity, and that obscurity indeed does not admit of understanding

headnotes.la: per ipsos locutus est; nunc quidem historice, nunc allegorice, nunc tropologice, nunc anagogice verba commiscens
headnotes.en: he spoke through them; now indeed historically, now allegorically, now tropologically, now anagogically, mingling his words

headnotes.la: quem de sinu Patris emissum, per matris viscera prolatum, mundus audivit docentem et dicentem
headnotes.en: whom, sent forth from the bosom of the Father, brought forth through the womb of his mother, the world heard teaching and saying

headnotes.la: Item illud,
headnotes.en: And likewise that,

headnotes.la: …ordes, beati mundo corde, beati pacifici, beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, ipsorum enim est regnum coelorum. Viderunt et opera mira dictu, venientem ad se leprosum, cui dixit Jesus
headnotes.en: …blessed are the peacemakers, blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. They saw also works wonderful to tell: a leper coming to him, to whom Jesus said

headnotes.la: et confestim mundata est lepra ejus [n: (ibid., 13)]: dicentem etiam centurioni
headnotes.en: and forthwith his leprosy was cleansed [n: (ibid., 13)]: saying also to the centurion

headnotes.la: …ibus*.] in aeterna vita repromittentem, quid nisi mirari, stupescere, et credere, et adorare potuerunt? Ab ipso vero audientes, quod in die ultimo cuncta ad judicium adducturus est, et bonis dicturus,
headnotes.en: …himself in life eternal: what could they do but marvel, be astonished, and believe, and adore? And hearing from him that on the last day he will bring all things to judgment, and will say to the good,

headnotes.la: …ut sic Evangelium adimplerent. Recte ergo haec omnis anima liquefacta est, ut Dilectus locutus est. Nihil enim est quod Pater plus Filio diligat, cui sua voce in Baptismo testimonium perhibet, dicens,
headnotes.en: …l. Rightly therefore has every such soul melted, when the Beloved spoke. For there is nothing that the Father loves more than the Son, to whom he bears witness by his own voice at his Baptism, saying,

headnotes.la: …st, quod ipsa ad vocem Dilecti liquefacta est; unde possit intelligi, se ipsum comprehendisse, et ex amica hac locutione suis finem laboribus invenisse. Quod ne quis corde concipiat, adnectit, dicens,
headnotes.en: …ce of the Beloved; whence it might be understood that she had comprehended him, and had from this friendly speech found an end to her labours. Lest anyone conceive this in his heart, she adds, saying,

headnotes.la: Omnes enim electae animae hunc quaerunt; ejus praesentiae [cn: 62* | F. add. *una cum*.] suis suscitatae corporibus assistere cupiunt; quod quia nondum est, sed certissime futurum repromittitur, ait,
headnotes.en: For all the elect souls seek him; they desire, being raised again in their bodies, to stand by his presence; and because this is not yet, but is most certainly promised as to come, she says,

headnotes.la: …us, et ad ipsum anhelamus, imponi fidem desideravi. Hunc quidem optavi, nec tamen inveni, quia usque ad diem praefinitum a Patre ejus erit exspectatio, et omnium certa remuneratio. Scriptum tamen est,
headnotes.en: …and pant after him. Him indeed I longed for, yet I did not find him, because until the day appointed by the Father there shall be the waiting for him, and the certain reward of all. Yet it is written,

headnotes.la: …taque Dominus in medio circuli residens, uno tueatur intuitu, quae fuerunt, quae sunt, et quae futura sunt, sibi cuncta haec praesentia judicantur, a quo uno intuitu, perspicue contuentur. Ait itaque,
headnotes.en: …the circle, beholds with one glance the things which have been, which are, and which are to come, all these are judged present to him, by whom in one glance they are clearly beheld. He says therefore,

headnotes.la: …ultiplicatis precibus, ut in illa detur sanctorum sibi gloria suscipi; ille quidem, cum illa dies aderit, hoc accepturus, hoc inventurus, et in illam gloriam vere introducendus est, de qua dictum est,
headnotes.en: … be granted him to be received into that glory of the saints; he indeed, when that day shall be at hand, is to receive this, to find this, and to be truly brought into that glory, of which it is said,

headnotes.la: Clamat utique ad Deum omnis anima electa, dicens,
headnotes.en: Assuredly every elect soul cries to God, saying,

headnotes.la: ut si quando tentat qui malignus est, ei vestra obstet gratia, ne ad effectum peccati perducat, quod ipso instigante conceptum est. Addit etiam,
headnotes.en: that if at any time he that is malignant tempts, your grace may withstand him, lest he bring to the effect of sin that which was conceived at his instigation. He adds also,

headnotes.la: …s est quem quaesivit, nec respondit ei qui vocatus est. Unde jure dici poterat et aestimari, quod eam Sponsus suo reliquerat consilio, et transeuntibus occupandam jure permiserit; quod removet dicens,
headnotes.en: …answer her. Whence it might rightly be said and reckoned that the Bridegroom had left her to her own counsel, and had by right suffered her to be seized by those passing by; which she removes, saying,

headnotes.la: …devote suscipiunt. His vitae verba praedicant, in his si qua supersunt peccata, mortificant, et in eo quem susceperunt, jam divinitatis amore amplius et acrius inflammant. Hoc itaque est quod dicitur,
headnotes.en: …ds of life, in these they mortify whatever sins remain, and in him whom they have received they now kindle them more fully and more keenly with the love of the Godhead. This therefore is what is said,

headnotes.la: Illa enim verba bene percutiunt, quae peccata occidunt; et illa bene vulnerant, quae amorem Dei jam conceptum, amplius inardescere faciunt, et magnificant
headnotes.en: For those words strike well which slay sins; and those wound well which make the love of God already conceived to burn more fully, and magnify it

headnotes.la: …clesiae tollunt, fidem in ea firmantes, spem roborantes, charitatem in ea radicantes, ut nihil jam sit, terrena haec quaeque despicere, dum soli Christo possit adhaerere. Et hoc quidem est quod dicit,
headnotes.en: … faith in her, strengthening hope, rooting charity in her, so that it is now nothing to despise all these earthly things, while she is able to cleave to Christ alone. And this indeed is what she says,

headnotes.la: …ec terrena substantia, quae propter Ecclesiam creata est: hac Ecclesia se protegit, se munit. Hanc vero totam deserit atque contemnit, cum jam Deo dari et appropinquari se conspicit. Orat ergo dicens,
headnotes.en: …e: with this the Church protects herself, fortifies herself. But she forsakes and despises the whole of it, when she now sees herself given to God and drawing near to him. She prays therefore, saying,

headnotes.la: id est, Virtutes coelestes, quae hujus miseriae participes in nullo estis, quae soli Jerusalem coelesti totum debetis quod estis, quod sapitis, quod nos protegitis;
headnotes.en: that is, ye heavenly Virtues, who are in nothing partakers of this misery, who owe wholly to the heavenly Jerusalem alone what you are, what you savour, that you protect us;

headnotes.la: (quod quidem certum est quod invenietis),
headnotes.en: (which indeed it is certain that you will find),

headnotes.la: …tis hujus Dilecto nuncient, ne errent, ne amorem forte datum alteri, praesentent alteri, sciscitantur quo signo suum cognoscant Dilectum, ne ab eis in incertum deferatur amoris nuncium. Dicunt itaque,
headnotes.en: … they err, lest they present to one the love perchance given to another, inquire by what sign they may know her Beloved, lest the message of love be borne by them into uncertainty. They say therefore,

headnotes.la: …am, quia nihil est spiritualis pulchritudinis, quo anima in hac vita Deo placere possit, quod non habeat Ecclesia in se, quod non repraesentet ex se. Illam non curat pulchritudinem de qua ait Salomon,
headnotes.en: …g of spiritual beauty whereby a soul in this life may please God, which the Church has not in herself, which she does not represent out of herself. She cares not for that beauty of which Solomon says,

headnotes.la: illam vero quae sequitur,
headnotes.en: but that which follows,

headnotes.la: …irtutes sunt quae ex timore, multae quae ex amore proveniunt; quas quidem omnes si numeres, has in Ecclesia nobile quidem munus, quod Deo praesentari dignum sit, invenies. Hanc ergo digne sic nominat,
headnotes.en: …y which spring from love; and if thou shouldst number them all, thou wilt find these in the Church a noble gift indeed, such as is worthy to be presented to God. Worthily therefore she thus names her,

headnotes.la: …llum quem diligis, et agnoscamus Patrem ejus a quo missus est, quem et tu diligis. Quod quia valde divinum est, et utriusque naturae in Christo capacissimum, geminat interrogationem suam, dicens item,
headnotes.en: …ovest, and may know his Father by whom he was sent, whom thou also lovest. And because this is exceedingly divine, and most capacious of both natures in Christ, she doubles her question, saying again,

headnotes.la: Haec Dilecti descriptio est, quam sub [cn: 63 | F. *binario*.] duodenario comprehendit numero, dicens,
headnotes.en: This is the description of the Beloved, which she comprehends under the number twelve, saying,

headnotes.la: in quo geminam in Christo Jesu Domino nostro comprehendit naturam: unam, quae divina est; alteram, quae est humana. Divinam quidem comprehendit, dicens,
headnotes.en: wherein she comprehends the twofold nature in Christ Jesus our Lord: the one, which is divine; the other, which is human. The divine indeed she comprehends, saying,

headnotes.la: humanam vero, addens,
headnotes.en: but the human, adding,

headnotes.la: … diu miseratus humanam, post annorum plura millia descendit in Virginem, et ex ipsa sumens carnem, sibique creans animam, homo factus venit in mundum, de mundo sibi quosdam eligens, quibus ipse dixit,
headnotes.en: …ame down into the Virgin, and taking flesh from her, and creating for himself a soul, being made man he came into the world, choosing out of the world certain men for himself, to whom he himself said,

headnotes.la: …tibus, coelum postmodum potenter ascendit. Hic in cruce positus, quia suo sanguine, cujus rubor color est, mundum redemit, merito rubicundus dictus est; ita ut in ejus memoriam et laudem Sponsa dicat,
headnotes.en: …ghtily ascended into heaven. He, being set upon the cross, because he redeemed the world by his blood, whose colour is red, is deservedly called ruddy; so that in his memory and praise the Bride says,

headnotes.la: addat etiam,
headnotes.en: and adds also,

headnotes.la: …t potuit, qui culpas hominum tergeret, qui culpas hominum non haberet, sed esset ut agnus innocens, qui mundi peccata tolleret, et innocentia sua noxas omnium in se credentium evacuaret; de quo David,
headnotes.en: …should not have the faults of men, but should be as an innocent lamb, who should take away the sins of the world, and by his innocence do away the guilt of all that believe in him; of whom David says,

headnotes.la: de quo Isaias,
headnotes.en: of whom Isaias says,

headnotes.la: …ncipit a capite ejus commendatio, quod auro comparatur. Nam sicut aurum optimum cunctis concupiscibilibus pretiosius est; ita et Deus omnibus quae concupisci et desiderari possunt, pretiosior occurrit
headnotes.en: … begins from his head, which is compared to gold. For as the finest gold is more precious than all things desirable; so also God is found more precious than all things which can be coveted and desired

headnotes.la: …tes, fideles sunt, Deo in omnibus obedientes, mandata ejus servantes, et quod dicto praedicant, facto id adimplentes, sicque in pugna vitae hujus, victoriam se palmae obtinuisse gratulantes. Sequitur,
headnotes.en: … in all things, keeping his commandments, and fulfilling in deed what they preach in word, and thus rejoicing that in the battle of this life they have obtained the victory of the palm. There follows,

headnotes.la: Id est, viri spirituales, qui ad videnda ejus mysteria perspicaces et acuti sunt, sunt
headnotes.en: That is, spiritual men, who are clear-sighted and keen to see his mysteries, are

headnotes.la: Lac quidem quo has lavari oportet, rationabilis sensus est sine dolo; unde dictum est,
headnotes.en: The milk indeed wherewith these must be washed is the reasonable sense without guile; whence it is said,

headnotes.la: [n: (I Petr. II, 2.)]
headnotes.en: [n: (I Petr. II, 2.)]

headnotes.la: …m sanguis egreditur, dum se minus juste dixisse aliquid vel fecisse quis verecundatur. His verba formantur quae Christum edocent, et illi credere, illum corde sequi et opere nos oportere praemonstrant
headnotes.en: …d that he has said or done something less justly. By these are formed the words which teach Christ, and show beforehand that we ought to believe in him, and to follow him in heart and in work. But the

headnotes.la: vero quae
headnotes.en: which

headnotes.la: iis, scilicet, qui pigmentorum vires dignoscunt,
headnotes.en: namely, by those who discern the powers of the perfumes,

headnotes.la: … rude erat et incompositum, hoc aptissimae reddat formae jam levigatum: huic leprosus offerebatur, et verbo uno curabatur; offerebatur mortuus, et uno verbo curatus abibat vivus. Recte ergo manus ejus
headnotes.en: … he renders into a most fitting form: to him a leper was offered, and by one word was cured; a dead man was offered, and, cured by one word, went away alive. Rightly therefore are his hands understood

headnotes.la: id est, leviter curantes, intelliguntur, quae solo sic verbo cuncta operantur, ut nunc esse melius quam fuerant advertantur. Unde et additur,
headnotes.en: that is, curing lightly, which so work all things by a word alone, that they are now perceived to be better than they had been. Whence also it is added,

headnotes.la: Hyacinthus enim lapis est, cujus color coeli est quando serenum est. Ut haec igitur omnia de coelo esse intelligas, et in terris coeli virtutem non ambigas, adjunctum est,
headnotes.en: …tone whose colour is that of the sky when it is clear. Therefore, that thou mayest understand all these things to be of heaven, and mayest not doubt of the power of heaven upon earth, there is joined,

headnotes.la: … pars nostri corporis est, quae levius suscipit laesionem; unde et hic eam Domini naturam significat, humanam, scilicet, qua laedi, qua infirmari, qua cruci quoque affligi potuit, ut de eo dictum est,
headnotes.en: … whence here it signifies that nature of the Lord, the human, namely, wherein he could be hurt, wherein he could be made weak, wherein he could also be afflicted with the cross, as it was said of him,

headnotes.la: Qui tamen venter hic dicitur
headnotes.en: Which belly nevertheless is here called

headnotes.la: … tempore, de candido fit rubicundum. Quae quidem omnia Christo competunt; ejus enim candor castitatis incomparabilis exstitit, cui nullus in filiis hominum aequari potuit, testante Psalmista, qui ait,
headnotes.en: …es ruddy. All which things indeed befit Christ; for his whiteness of chastity stood forth incomparable, to which none among the sons of men could be made equal, the Psalmist bearing witness, who says,

headnotes.la: … quia nullum in ea, quo teneretur, peccatum fuit: caro quoque in sepulchro post mortem nil pertulit, quia utrimque peccatum abfuit, quo et corruptela, et animae calumnia possit adjici. Unde Psalmista,
headnotes.en: …be held: his flesh also in the sepulchre after death suffered nothing, because on either side sin was absent, whereby both corruption and a charge against the soul might be added. Whence the Psalmist,

headnotes.la: …altum, in longum quoque usque ad Oceanum Orientalem extendens: praecipuae ejus arbores, cupressus, et cedrus sunt; quorum folia albicantia silvae nomen praestant, ut Libanus dicatur; est enim Libanus,
headnotes.en: …f on high, in length also as far as the Eastern Ocean: its chief trees are the cypress and the cedar, whose whitening leaves furnish the name of the wood, so that it is called Libanus; for Libanus is,

headnotes.la: …s attribuitur, qui candor est animarum, et omnium oblectatio virtutum, ad quem qui pervenerit, nulla sibi ad humana redeundi voluntas est, nulla in anima praeteritorum recordatio. Quare? quia ipse est
headnotes.en: …whiteness of souls, and the delight of all the virtues, unto whom he that has come has no will of returning to human things, no remembrance in his soul of things past. Wherefore? because he himself is

headnotes.la: Quid hoc gutture, nisi Novi Testamenti emissio, designatur? Praecessit enim Vetus, quo dictum est
headnotes.en: What is designated by this throat, unless the sending forth of the New Testament? For the Old went before, wherein it was said

headnotes.la: et caetera quae sequuntur. Novo vero quid dictum est?
headnotes.en: and the rest which follow. [var: Vulg. *reddet animam pro anima*, without a subject "man"] But in the New what has been said?

headnotes.la: Quid hoc dulcius? quid suavius esse potest? Totum vero Testamentum Novum si consideres, nil nisi quod dulce est et desiderabile prorsus invenies. His dictis, sequitur,

headnotes.la: …dem Dei Filius foris inventus est, id est, in hac forma corporali, quam de novo assumpsit, et in ipsa mundo apparuit, et in hac ab eo (ut dictum est) osculum sibi reconciliationis assumpsit; unde ait,
headnotes.en: …without, that is, in this bodily form, which he newly took, and in it appeared to the world, and in this he received to himself from him (as has been said) the kiss of reconciliation; whence she says,

headnotes.la: …tur. At postquam morte unigeniti reconciliatus est, Infernum deserens, regionem Paradisi possidere coepit et coeli, et extunc nec coeli possessoribus despectui habitus est, nec Inferni. Ait enim ipsa,
headnotes.en: … forsaking Hell, he began to possess the region of Paradise and of heaven, and from thenceforth he was held in contempt neither by the possessors of heaven, nor by those of Hell. For she herself says,

headnotes.la: id est, firmissimo amplexu tenebo te: non minis, non verberibus, non omni mortis genere amovebor aut avellar a te: et sic inducam te
headnotes.en: that is, I will hold thee with a most firm embrace: not by threats, not by stripes, not by every kind of death shall I be removed or torn away from thee: and thus will I bring thee

headnotes.la: coelestis, scilicet, Jerusalem, quae erudit me, et exemplum mihi dilectionis ostendit, qua semper adhaeream tibi, et amoveri nequeam a te; et inducam te in
headnotes.en: namely of the heavenly Jerusalem, which instructs me, and shews me the example of that love whereby I may always cleave to thee, and may not be able to be removed from thee; and I will bring thee into

headnotes.la: …lud amoris habitaculum, quo te semper tenuit genitrix mea, id est, antiquissima de patriarchis et prophetis, aliisque fidelibus exorta collectio, et, quae nunquam a te avelli potuit, sacra congregatio
headnotes.en: …bore me has ever held thee, that is, that most ancient gathering sprung from the patriarchs and the prophets and the other faithful, and that holy congregation which could never be torn away from thee

headnotes.la: quia tunc erimus omnes docibiles Dei. Et nos quid tibi dabimus?
headnotes.en: because then shall we all be taught of God. And what shall we give thee?

headnotes.la: amorem, scilicet, sempiternum; qui tot modis formatus est, quod modis vina formari solent ex diversis speciebus;
headnotes.en: namely everlasting love; which is formed in so many ways, as wines are wont to be formed from divers kinds;

headnotes.la: …scendunt, et sic, quae sit eis patria destinata, cognoscunt. Hoc desertum est locus iste, quem Dominus ascendendo deseruit, cum multis videntibus in coelum elevatus ascendit. Quare sequitur, haec ipsa
headnotes.en: …is destined for them. This desert is that place which the Lord deserted by ascending, when, in the sight of many, he was lifted up and ascended into heaven. Wherefore it follows, that this same one is

headnotes.la: Dictum est, quod ista deliciis affluens, super Dilectum suum innixa est: jam, quod illi inniti potuerit et debuerit, consequenter demonstratur. Ait enim,
headnotes.en: It has been said that she, flowing with delights, is leaning upon her Beloved: now it is consequently shewn that she could and ought to lean upon him. For he says,

headnotes.la: …onsus iste crucem sustinens, omnes eripuit, ideoque seipsam sub malo, id est, sub peccato quod ex malo contractum est, positam suscitasse et redemisse confitetur. Quod ne modicum aestimetur, adjungit,
headnotes.en: …and therefore he confesses that he raised up and redeemed her, placed under the apple, that is, under the sin which was contracted from the apple. And that this be not esteemed a small thing, he adds,

headnotes.la: …t, in corde tuo; ut in omni eo quod agere disposueris, hanc semper attendas dilectionem, ne quid effectu complere praesumas, nisi id huic dilectioni cohaerere conspicias. Idem et de brachio subjungit,
headnotes.en: …hou shalt have purposed to do thou attend always to this love, that thou presume not to fulfil anything in act, unless thou see it to cleave to this love. The same also he subjoins concerning the arm,

headnotes.la: …si ambo memoriale hujus dilectionis teneant, ab omni se opere, quod huic non convenit dilectioni, cohibebunt. Sic cor muniens et brachia, hoc quod alias dictum est, persuadet: alias namque dictum est,
headnotes.en: …al of this love, they will restrain themselves from every work which suits not this love. Thus fortifying the heart and the arms, he urges that which has been said elsewhere: for elsewhere it is said,

headnotes.la: … iis honoribus, et eosdem cupientes, se quasi sequaces martyrum et ipsorum imitatores praeferebant, et sic se martyres, aut quasi martyres aestimabant: quorum studia Sponsus ipse sic improbat, dicens,
headnotes.en: …ut themselves forward as though followers of the martyrs and imitators of them, and thus esteemed themselves martyrs, or as it were martyrs: whose zeal the Bridegroom himself thus disapproves, saying,

headnotes.la: …nt hanc charitatem extinguere: hanc enim dilectionem tribulationes nullae, nullae vexationum adinventiones possunt extinguere; quia quo mala multiplicantur, in Deum hinc constat ipsum excrescere, quia
headnotes.en: …s cannot quench this charity: for no tribulations, no devices of vexations can quench this love; because, the more evils are multiplied, the more it is certain that it grows up hence into God, because

headnotes.la: …ommonuit, et quod hoc memoriale cordis habeat, edocta; edocta quoque quod charitas vincat omnia; ipsa quidem omnia grata habet et suscipit; et jam de charitate commonita, quaestionem annectit, dicens,
headnotes.en: …e this memorial of the heart; taught also that charity conquers all things; she indeed holds all things pleasing and receives them; and now, admonished concerning charity, she adds a question, saying,

headnotes.la: Venit sibi in mentem, quod ait Apostolus,
headnotes.en: There comes to her mind what the Apostle says,

headnotes.la: … itaque sanctum apostolum in novissimis convertendam, et Eliam, et Henoch ad hos convertendos a Christo reservatos praesciens, hanc propter conversionem futuram sororem nominans, ex charitate sic ait,
headnotes.en: …mes [by] the holy apostle, and that Elias and Henoch have been reserved by Christ for the converting of these, and naming her sister on account of the conversion to come, she thus says out of charity,

headnotes.la: …am nulla. Haec ubera non habet, nulla in se doctrinae retinacula continet; quae propter se facta sunt, haec negat et reticet. Hanc ergo ad fidem in novissimo venturam praesciens, a Sponso sic quaerit,
headnotes.en: …ands of doctrine; the things which were done for her sake, these she denies and keeps silent about. Foreknowing therefore that she shall come to the faith at the last, she thus asks of the Bridegroom,

headnotes.la: …os propugnacula argentea, id est, divinarum scripturarum eis dentur testimonia, et autoritatum quibus praemunimur; his donentur insignia, quibus hi jam muniti Ecclesiae verae sunt defensores et tutela
headnotes.en: … Scriptures be given them, and of the authorities wherewith we are fortified; that the ensigns be granted to these, whereby these, now fortified, are the defenders and the safeguard of the true Church

headnotes.la: …diti scripturis, quibus non summa proponenda sunt, et intellectu difficilia, sed tabulae compingendae sunt cedrinae, id est, leves Scripturae proponendae; ut est ea tabula quam pinxit Dominus, dicens,
headnotes.en: …t to be set forth, nor things difficult of understanding, but boards of cedar are to be joined together, that is, light Scriptures are to be set forth; as is that board which the Lord painted, saying,

headnotes.la: Audito Dilecti responso, quo Sponsam monet, ut et conversae synagogae propugnacula proponat argentea, et ad defensionem Ecclesiae propugnatores mittat idoneos, ipsa congratulanter ait,
headnotes.en: …the Beloved being heard, wherein he admonishes the Bride both to set forth bulwarks of silver for the converted synagogue, and to send fit defenders for the defence of the Church, she gratefully says,

headnotes.la: …a nomino, quod meo eos lacte nutrio, hi mecum erunt Ecclesiae firma et inexpugnabilis defensio, et mecum aeternae vitae incontradicibilis acquisitio; eo quod reddita jam mihi sorore mea quae perierat,
headnotes.en: … my milk, these shall be with me the firm and unassailable defence of the Church, and with me the incontestable acquiring of eternal life; in that, my sister who had perished being now restored to me,

headnotes.la: …ntici hujus, et consummata plenitudine Sponsae hujus, cum sibi synagoga, quam sororem nominat, ad fidem conversa erit, et ad fidem Gentium plenitudo intraverit, de se tota jam Sponsa loquitur, dicens,
headnotes.en: …ynagogue, which she names her sister, shall have been converted to the faith for her, and the fulness of the Gentiles shall have entered into the faith, the Bride now speaks of herself entire, saying,

headnotes.la: …go quidem cum plenitudine Gentium jam vocata, cum synagoga jam ad fidem conversa, exstiti vinea pacifico, id est, Jesu Christo Domino nostro, qui pacificavit omnia quae in terra sunt, et quae in coelo
headnotes.en: … synagogue now converted to the faith, have stood forth a vineyard to the peaceable one, that is, to Jesus Christ our Lord, who has made peace with all things that are in earth, and that are in heaven

headnotes.la: id est, in multitudine Gentium, quae tota a Deo creata est, sed non tota ad vitam praeordinata;
headnotes.en: that is, in the multitude of the Gentiles, which was wholly created by God, but not wholly foreordained unto life;

headnotes.la: …coluit, plantavit, et secuit, et ad florem, fructumque perduxit; quae non in amaritudinem conversa est, nec labruscas fecit, sed elegantes uvas, et Deo Patri praesentari dignissimas. Unde hic dicitur,
headnotes.en: …ought through to flower and to fruit; which was not turned into bitterness, nor brought forth wild grapes, but choice grapes, and most worthy to be presented to God the Father. Whence here it is said,

headnotes.la: Quis iste vir est? Vir ille bonus, cujus meminit David, dicens,
headnotes.en: Who is this man? That good man whom David calls to mind, saying,

headnotes.la: …hunc in infinitum numerus extenditur, habens millenarium sibi semper radicem et unitatem. Bene ergo per hunc, infinitas; et per argentum, beatitudinis excellentia demonstratur; de hac enim dictum est,
headnotes.en: …er is extended to infinity, having always the thousand for its root and unity. Well therefore by this is infinity shewn, and by the silver, the excellence of beatitude; for concerning this it is said,

headnotes.la: …Spiritus examinatum, quo nihil dulcius tinnit eloquio, nihil animae plus sapidum; quo nil a terra probatius, quo nil igne septiformis spiritus purgatius invenitur: de qua responsum hoc Patris accipit,
headnotes.en: …is more savoury to the soul; than which nothing is found more proved from the earth, nothing more purified by the fire of the sevenfold Spirit: concerning which she receives this answer of the Father,

headnotes.la: Haec Sponsi est ultima commonitio, qua Sponsam de laude sua commonet, dicens,
headnotes.en: This is the last admonition of the Bridegroom, wherewith he admonishes the Bride concerning his praise, saying,

headnotes.la: …r, monitis coelestibus exposcitur, cum dicitur Quae habitas in hortis Ecclesiarum, fac me audire vocem tuam, ut a cunctis Ecclesiis laus mea resonet, et ab omni laus mea cum gratiarum actione resultet
headnotes.en: …hou that dwellest in the gardens of the Churches, make me hear thy voice, that my praise may resound from all the Churches, and that from every one my praise may ring back again with thanksgiving. For

headnotes.la: enim
Haec est Ecclesiae ultima responsio, qua respondet Sponsa Dilecto suo, dicens,
headnotes.en: This is the last answer of the Church, wherewith the Bride answers her Beloved, saying,

headnotes.la: … laudem personet, non quod velit, quod nunc cantica laudis incipiat, sed exspectata communi omnium resurrectione, cum Sponsus in nube venerit, cum ejus adventum angelus clara voce personuerit, dicens,
headnotes.en: …the canticles of praise, but the common resurrection of all being awaited, when the Bridegroom shall have come in a cloud, when an angel with a clear voice shall have sounded forth his coming, saying,

headnotes.la: …x stipatus Angelis, in sede suae majestatis sederit, et ei, nullo excepto, mundus occurrerit, et horrendam in reprobos sententiam tulerit, et dederit electis suis omnibus sententiam quam dicturus est,
headnotes.en: …esty, and the world, none excepted, shall have run to meet him, and he shall have borne a dreadful sentence upon the reprobate, and shall have given to all his elect the sentence which he is to speak,

headnotes.la: … a seculo, cunctique ejus laudis participes in secula benedicentur a Domino. Quod quia diligenti se Sponsae praemonstratum est, ideo non indignando, sed moram hanc patienter sustinendo, sic respondet,
headnotes.en: …aise shall be blessed by the Lord unto the ages. And because this was shewn beforehand to the Bride that loves him, therefore, not with indignation, but bearing this delay patiently, she thus answers,

headnotes.la: …e cervorum, quae munda quidem animalia sunt, et a conspectibus hominum se in jugis montium continentia. Quos quidem montes, ubi iste cervorum hinnulus habitat, ut a caeteris montibus discernat, addit,
headnotes.en: …and keep themselves from the sight of men upon the ridges of the mountains. Which mountains indeed, where this fawn of the harts dwells, that he may distinguish them from the other mountains, he adds,

proseNotes.raw: (Nam totum quod in osculo misera peccat, et carnalis affectio, ab ejus mente tam longe est, quam ipsa procul a vitio, virtute purificata, secessit.)
